explanations.plan: P3 with more payments overtime and general break delays
explanations.text:
Approve R1: outage message, chat deflection, callback, break delays on both queues and overtime for 55 payments agents. Predicted 83.2% service level for 10:45-12:45 at ₹10,275.
The spike is caused by the UPI switch outage (P1 incident INC-20261006-6998, opened 10:31), not by a staffing problem. Payments calls hit 213 against 111.9 forecast (+90%), and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Service level fell to 4.7%, with 59 calls abandoned, even though staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents). R1 cuts demand with the outage message, 20% chat deflection of payment_status_enquiry and callback. It adds capacity with overtime for 55 payments agents, delayed breaks on both queues and cancelled payments coaching. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the disruption window: payments 86.6%, general 77.5%, abandon rate 3.7%, rest of day 89.2%. There are no policy violations and no escalation is needed.
Trade-off: P3 (₹7,575) is ₹2,700 cheaper but reaches only 77.5%, just short of target, with 5.2% abandons.
Trade-off: R2 (₹11,355) reaches 88.0% and lifts general to 91.1%, but costs ₹1,080 more than R1 for a result already above target.
Trade-off: Under R1 the general queue sits at 77.5%, below 80%. Its breaks are delayed to protect it, but it is the weaker queue.
Trade-off: Doing nothing (P0) leaves service level at 29.4% with 22.2% abandons. The low-cost plans P1 and P2 only reach 39.5% and 49.8%.
Trade-off: Staffing-only (P4) costs ₹8,265 for just 52.6%. Overtime without the demand-cutting levers is poor value.
Watch: Track the UPI incident status. If it is resolved early, release overtime and turn off the outage message. If it runs past 12:45, re-plan. Check that enough of the 55 payments agents actually accept overtime from 11:15, and watch the general queue's service level, which is forecast below target at 77.5%.

explanations.plan: No-cost: break shifts, callback and extended outage message
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost break shifts, IVR callbacks and an extended UPI outage message, predicted to lift service level to 85.5% for 11:30-13:30 against the 80% target.
The surge is driven by the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls hit 213 at 10:30 against 111.9 forecast, and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are fine, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. Doing nothing (P0) only just clears the target overall at 80.4%, and general would sit at 71.6%. P1 costs nothing and breaks no policy. It raises the window service level to 85.5% (payments 90.2%, general 78.1%), cuts abandons from 4.8% to 3.5% and lifts rest-of-day to 93.7%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target.
Trade-off: General queue stays below 80% at 78.1% under P1. P2 (₹720) brings it to 84.5% and P3 (₹3,960) to 89.0%.
Trade-off: P2 adds chat deflection for ₹720, giving 89.4% overall and 2.9% abandons. That is a modest gain for a small cost if general matters.
Trade-off: P3 overtime for 20 agents gives the best result (91.7%, 1.9% abandons) but costs ₹3,960 and depends on agents accepting the offer.
Trade-off: Delaying breaks by 30-45 minutes puts extra strain on agents during a busy period.
Watch: Watch the general queue, which is the weak spot at a predicted 78.1%. If it trends lower, or the UPI incident runs past 13:30, consider moving to P2. Keep the outage message in line with incident updates and remove it once UPI recovers. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Demand cut, breaks moved past the peak, peak overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (demand cut, breaks moved past the peak, peak overtime for 21 payments agents 13:30-14:30) at ₹4,284, and bring in the duty manager. It is the best available plan but is predicted at only 57.1% against the 80% target for 13:00-15:00.
The surge comes from the UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents) and handle time is below forecast, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. R2 tackles both sides. It cuts demand with an IVR outage message and 20% chat deflection on both queues. It adds capacity with overtime concentrated on the 13:30-14:30 peak and moves breaks out of the peak to 14:00-15:00. Predicted service level for 13:00-15:00 is 57.1% (payments 50.1%, general 71.0%), with abandons at 10.2%. Doing nothing gives 30.8% and 21.7% abandons. Rest-of-day service level improves to 82.1%. No plan reaches 80%, and R2 has the highest predicted service level of all options. Escalation is flagged under ESC-02 because 57% is below the 70% escalation line. The duty manager should be involved to consider further measures beyond this plan.
Trade-off: R1 costs ₹360 more (₹4,644) for slightly worse results: 56.6% overall, 10.6% abandons. It spreads overtime over 1.5 h rather than the peak hour.
Trade-off: P3 (₹3,732) is cheaper but reaches only 47.9%, with payments at 41.7% and abandons at 12.0%.
Trade-off: P2 (₹492) and P4 (₹2,880) reach only 39.7% and 38.2%. The no-cost P1 is no better than doing nothing (29.9%).
Trade-off: The general queue holds at 71.0% under R2, versus 56.2% with no action. It depends on chat deflection and on breaks moving to 14:00-15:00.
Watch: Track uptake of the 21 overtime offers before 13:30 and whether payments service level is recovering in the 13:30-14:30 intervals. Watch for general-queue service level slipping when the delayed breaks land at 14:00-15:00. Follow INC-20261006-6998 for resolution, which would end the excess upi_payment_failed demand.

explanations.plan: P3 overtime kept, break delay dropped, chat widened to payments
explanations.text:
Approve R2: keep overtime on general (25 agents 10:15-12:15, 22 agents 12:15-14:15) and widen chat deflection to both queues. Predicted service level is 88.9% for 10:15-14:45 against the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹17,508.
The 09:00 personal loan email (MKT-2026-551) is driving extra calls on general: 307 calls against 236 forecast over the last four intervals, mostly loan and new-offer enquiries. Service level has already fallen to 68%. This is a demand problem, not a staffing problem. Doing nothing would leave the window at 50% (general 38.4%) with 12.3% abandons. R2 lifts the window to 88.9%, with general at 88.3% and payments at 89.6%. Abandons drop to 2.6% and the rest of the day reaches 92.6%. It is the cheapest option that meets the target with no policy issues. It also drops the break delay, so agents get their breaks on time.
Trade-off: The cheaper options all miss the 80% target. P3 (₹14,868) reaches 77.9%, P4 (₹9,720) reaches 70.1%, and P1 and P2 (₹0 and ₹468) reach only 45.6-49.0%.
Trade-off: R1 performs almost the same (88.8%, 2.5% abandons) but costs ₹180 more (₹17,688). Its overtime blocks overlap, which needs more scheduling.
Trade-off: Payments is protected under R2 at 89.6%, compared with 76.3% under P3. Widening chat deflection to payments enquiries keeps the overtime on general from leaving payments short.
Watch: Check by 10:45 that the overtime has been taken up close to the 25 agents planned and that chat deflection is reaching about 20% of the targeted enquiries. If campaign calls keep climbing above the current pattern, or general stays below 80% after the first hour, reassess. Plan for the 12:15 overtime handover of 22 agents.

explanations.plan: Break shift plus afternoon overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (break shift plus afternoon overtime, ₹720), but involve the duty manager now: even the best compliant plan only reaches about 66% against the 80% target.
The general queue is running above forecast because of the MKT-2026-551 personal loan email sent at 09:00. Over the last four intervals there were 307 calls against 236 forecast, mostly loan_enquiry (92 vs 40) and new_offer_enquiry (50 vs 14), and service level fell to 68% at 09:45. This is extra demand, not a staffing shortfall. R2 delays general and payments breaks from 12:30-13:00 by 45 minutes, offers overtime to 11 general agents 14:00-16:00 and moves 4 cross-skilled agents from payments to general 15:00-16:00. It is predicted at 66.2% for 11:00-15:15 (general 59.8%, payments 74.5%) with 6.5% abandons, and 77.9% for the rest of the day. That is the best of the policy-compliant plans, but only marginally better than doing nothing (66.0%). Escalation is required under ESC-02 because the best compliant plan is below the 70% line.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) costs nothing and is predicted at 66.0%, almost the same as R2. The ₹720 buys very little on the overall figure.
Trade-off: R1 costs the same ₹720 and gives general slightly more help (61.0% vs 59.8%). It is 65.9% overall and takes more from payments (72.3% vs 74.5%).
Trade-off: P1 is free but predicted lower at 63.7%. P4 costs ₹1,305 and reaches only 64.2%. Both are worse than R2.
Trade-off: P2 (₹225, 81.9%) and P3 (₹1,080, 82.3%) are the only plans that hit target, but they breach CX-01: a known-issue IVR message needs a confirmed outage or incident, and there is none. Only the duty manager could consider an alternative compliant message for these campaign calls.
Watch: Watch general queue service level and abandons through 11:00-15:15, and check that payments holds near 74.5% while its breaks are shifted and agents move across. Ask the duty manager whether marketing can pause or adjust the campaign, or whether a compliant campaign IVR message can be approved, as the staffing options alone will not get close to 80%.

explanations.plan: Policy-safe: chat deflection, coaching cancellation and more cross-skill moves
explanations.text:
Approve R1: the best policy-compliant plan, lifting service level to 76.6% for 13:45-17:30 for ₹2,703. It still falls short of the 80% target.
The extra calls come from the MKT-2026-551 loan email, not from a staffing problem. Over the last four intervals there were 307 calls against 236 forecast, mostly loan and new-offer enquiries, and service level fell to 68% at 09:45. With no action, the disruption window is predicted at 72.1%, with the general queue at 63.6%. R1 adds chat deflection on both queues, cancels coaching and moves up to 9 cross-skilled agents from payments to general. That raises the window to 76.6% (general 70.1%, payments 85.3%), cuts abandons from 7.9% to 6.0%, and puts the rest of the day at 81.5%. No policy-compliant option reaches 80% over the window.
Trade-off: P2 (80.1%, ₹732) and P3 (79.6%, ₹2,307) score higher or cost less. Both rely on an IVR outage message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same ₹2,703 and has slightly fewer abandons (5.6% vs 6.0%), but window service level is a little lower (76.4%, general 69.0%) and it delays breaks.
Trade-off: P1 is free but makes things worse: 69.7%, with general at 60.4%.
Trade-off: Moving agents off payments has little downside here: payments is predicted at 85.3% under R1, up from 83.7% with no action.
Watch: Watch the general queue. It is predicted at only 70.1% even with R1, so check that chat deflection is actually taking new-offer enquiries from 14:45. Keep payments above 80% once the 6-agent move starts at 16:00. If loan enquiries keep exceeding forecast, consider asking the duty manager about other options, such as asking marketing to clarify the campaign or a policy-compliant message.

explanations.plan: No-cost callback cover for the evening
explanations.text:
Approve P1: switch on IVR callback on both queues 18:00–20:00 at no extra cost; the disruption window is predicted at 95.5% against an 80% target.
The general queue is running 44% over forecast (2,409 calls vs 1,669) because of the 09:00 pre-approved loan email (MKT-2026-551). Loan and new-offer enquiries are 3–4x normal, and service level has dipped as low as 24% today. For 14:45–18:45 the model predicts the target is met even with no action (P0 at 95.3%). P1 adds evening callbacks for free, giving 95.5% overall, 92.9% on general and 98.0% on payments, with a 0.8% abandon rate. P1 follows policy, so it is the cheapest compliant plan.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) also costs nothing and predicts 95.3%. P1 gives slightly better window figures (95.5%, 0.8% abandon vs 0.9%) and puts evening callback cover in place at no cost. General is predicted fractionally lower under P1 (92.9% vs 93.4%), while payments improves (98.0% vs 97.1%).
Trade-off: P2 (₹144) and P3 (₹528) predict higher results (97.0% and 97.8%; rest of day 92.7% and 94.5%). Both break policy CX-01, because they would play a known-issue message when there is no confirmed outage or incident. A marketing campaign does not count.
Trade-off: P4 (chat deflection, ₹552) follows policy and predicts 96.3% (general 94.0%, rest of day 93.0%). It costs ₹552 for a target that P1 already meets for free.
Trade-off: With P1, rest of day stays at 89.6%, the same as doing nothing. The paid options lift it to 92.7–94.5%.
Watch: The forecast predicts 95.3% even with no action, yet general has run 35–74% over forecast in every interval since 12:45 and dipped as low as 24%. Check that the predictions reflect the campaign volume. If general calls keep running well above forecast or service level stays low, P4 is the compliant step up. No escalation is needed.

explanations.plan: Targeted overtime at the peak hours plus coaching
explanations.text:
Approve P3: targeted overtime at the peak hours, cancel coaching and offer callbacks on payments. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target (81.7%) for 08:30-15:15, at ₹12,900.
Payments has had 11 agents against 17 planned since 08:00. Most of the gap is lateness from the bus strike (8 agents), plus 1 sick. Call volume is near normal (+8.4%), so the problem is missing staff, not extra calls. General is also short (8 absences against a usual 2.4), so it can't lend agents to payments. Doing nothing leaves the window at 63.0%. The cheaper plans can't fix a staffing gap: P1 reaches only 63.2% and P2 only 71.5%. P3 adds overtime on both queues in the busiest hours. It lifts the window to 81.7% (payments 86.6%, general 75.3%), cuts abandons to 3.5% from 8.2%, and raises rest of day to 87.3%.
Trade-off: Cost: ₹12,900, against ₹2,652 for P2. P2 still misses target at 71.5%, with 5.5% of callers abandoning.
Trade-off: Other queue: general reaches only 75.3% under P3, below the 80% target, though up from 59.5% with no action. P4 brings general to 83.6% but costs ₹4,152 more (₹17,052).
Trade-off: Risk: the result depends on enough agents accepting overtime (up to 10 on payments and 8 on general per block). If uptake is short, the plan will fall back towards target or below it.
Trade-off: Coaching is cancelled for the whole window.
Watch: Track overtime acceptances by 10:00, and service level on general from 11:00. If payments uptake falls short, or general stays well below 75%, consider adding P4's chat deflection and general callbacks. Also check whether the late agents start arriving early as the strike eases, which would reduce the overtime needed.

explanations.plan: Low-cost demand relief: chat deflection and late coaching cancel
explanations.text:
Approve P2: chat deflection, delayed breaks, general callback and a cancelled late payments coaching session lift service level to 80.4% (target 80%) for ₹3,687.
Unplanned absence (bus-strike lateness plus sickness) has left both queues about 6–7 agents short while call volume is on plan. With no action, service level for 09:45–15:30 is predicted at 68.3%, with 6.8% abandons. P2 reduces demand by moving 20% of simple status and balance enquiries to chat, delays the 09:45–10:30 breaks by 45 minutes, adds callback on general and cancels the 15:30–16:00 payments coaching. The result is a predicted 80.4% service level (payments 78.5%, general 82.9%), abandons falling to 4.4%, and 85.7% for the rest of the day. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target and it breaks no policy.
Trade-off: P4 adds overtime on both queues for 82.9% (payments 81.8%) and 3.7% abandons, but costs ₹6,567, ₹2,880 more than P2, for a modest gain.
Trade-off: P3's payments-only overtime costs ₹2,880 but reaches only 69.8%, so extra staff alone does not close the gap at that scale.
Trade-off: P1 (no cost) does worse than no action, 65.9% vs 68.3%, so the breaks and callback only work when combined with deflection.
Trade-off: Payments stays slightly under target at 78.5% under P2, while general carries the overall figure at 82.9%.
Watch: Watch payments service level first, as it is the queue below 80%. Check that chat is absorbing the deflected enquiries without a backlog building. If the strike-delayed staff arrive, capacity will improve and you may be able to restore breaks or the coaching session. If payments keeps slipping, P4's payments overtime is the next step.

explanations.plan: Lean: overtime for the evening only, with chat deflection
explanations.text:
Approve P4 (Lean): evening overtime plus chat deflection lifts 16:15-20:00 service level to 84.0% against an 80% target, for ₹2,925.
Capacity is down on both queues because of absences, mostly bus-strike lateness (payments 19 absences vs a usual 2.6; general 10 vs 2.4). Call volume is not the problem. Doing nothing leaves the window at 75.9%, with payments at 69.4%. P4 cancels payments coaching from 16:15 to 17:30. It moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments from 17:00 to 18:00. It deflects 20% of status and balance enquiries to chat from 17:00 to 20:00. It offers overtime to 5 payments agents from 18:00 to 20:00 and adds a general callback from 18:00 to 19:00. Predicted results are payments 82.8%, general 85.5% and abandons 4.0%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target with no policy violations.
Trade-off: P3 (₹3,645) adds 0.4 points (84.4%) and cuts abandons to 3.7% vs 4.0%. That is ₹720 more for a marginal gain.
Trade-off: P2 (₹3,105) costs more than P4 and still misses the target at 79.1%, with payments at 76.0% and abandons at 5.7%.
Trade-off: P1 (₹225) is nearly free but makes things worse overall at 72.8%. Payments only reaches 71.1% and general drops to 75.0%.
Trade-off: Risk to general: moving 3 agents to payments still leaves general at 85.5%, comfortably above target.
Watch: Handle time on general has run 15% above forecast for the last two intervals. If that continues, general's margin after the agent move could shrink. Also confirm that 5 payments agents actually accept the 18:00-20:00 overtime. If fewer accept, payments could fall back below 80%. As strike-delayed agents arrive, staffing may recover, and you may be able to release overtime early.

explanations.plan: Maximum recovery: overtime, chat deflection and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P4 (overtime, chat deflection and callback): the only option predicted to reach the 80% target over 10:15-12:15, at 81.7% for ₹6,321.
Calls on general are running long because of the CRM search slowdown (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, searches taking 20–40 s). Handle time reached 646 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast. Volume and staffing are close to plan. Service level fell to 14.7% with 18 abandons in that interval. Doing nothing is predicted to give 58.3% over the window, with general at 33.8%. P4 combines the free levers (delayed breaks, cancelled coaching, 3 agents moved from payments for 10:15-11:00) with overtime for 30 general agents from 10:45-12:00, 20% chat deflection of balance and offer enquiries, and IVR callback until 11:45. It is predicted to lift the window to 81.7% and cut abandons to 4.3%. The rest of the day is expected to finish at 88.5%. No policy rules are broken.
Trade-off: Cost: P4 is the most expensive at ₹6,321. P3 (overtime for 25 agents, ₹4,575) saves ₹1,746 but reaches only 73.3% with 6.4% abandons, so it misses the target.
Trade-off: Cheaper options fall well short. P2 (chat deflection, ₹471) gives 65.4%. P1 (₹75) gives 57.5%, slightly below no action, because general drops to 26.7%.
Trade-off: General is still below target even under P4, at 69.3%. The overall 81.7% depends on payments being strong at 90.6%.
Trade-off: Payments is not put at risk: it stays at 90.6% despite lending 3 agents and delaying its breaks from 11:00-11:45.
Watch: Track handle time and the CRM incident. If search speed recovers, consider stopping overtime early to save cost. If the incident worsens or overtime take-up falls short of 30 agents, general will slip further and the plan should be reviewed.

explanations.plan: Balanced overtime + deflection
explanations.text:
Approve P3 (overtime + chat deflection + break delays + callbacks) for 12:00-14:00, and bring in the duty manager: it is the best available plan, but at 57.7% it still falls well short of the 80% target.
Calls on general are running long because CRM customer search is taking 20–40 seconds (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, opened 09:55). Handle time reached 646 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast, while volume and staffing are close to plan. Service level fell to 14.7% with 18 abandons in that interval. If we do nothing, 12:00-14:00 is predicted at 30.6% with 22.9% abandons. P3 offers overtime to 20 general and 12 payments agents from 12:30-14:30, delays breaks, adds IVR callback and 20% chat deflection on both queues. It lifts the window to 57.7% (general 59.2%, payments 56.6%), cuts abandons to 12.0% and raises rest-of-day to 85.7%, for ₹7,884. No plan reaches 80%. ESCALATION: P3 is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved, both to approve and to push for faster resolution of the CRM incident, which is the real fix.
Trade-off: R1 and R2 cost the same ₹7,884 and avoid break delays, but predict lower service: R1 56.9% (general only 53.3%) and R2 51.6%, with higher abandons (13.3% and 15.1%).
Trade-off: P4 is cheaper at ₹6,480 but reaches only 41.1% with 15.9% abandons.
Trade-off: P2 costs just ₹1,404 but reaches only 38.5%.
Trade-off: P1 is free but makes things worse than doing nothing (20.8%, general 10.9%).
Trade-off: P3 balances both queues, with neither queue left far behind.
Watch: Watch CRM search times and the incident status. If the slowness clears before 12:00, scale back the overtime. Also watch overtime take-up on both queues: P3's prediction assumes the 20 general and 12 payments agents accept. Track general handle time against the roughly 646 s seen at 10:00.

explanations.plan: Earlier break shift plus full bridge and overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R1 (₹624) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best policy-compliant plan, but it only lifts the 12:45–14:45 service level to 55.1% against an 80% target.
Calls on general are running long because of the CRM search slowness (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, searches taking 20–40 s). Handle time reached 646.0 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast, while volume and staffing are close to plan. With no action, the 12:45–14:45 window is predicted at 49.7%, with payments at 38.8% and 13.9% abandons. R1 combines several measures: overtime for 2 payments agents (13:15–14:15), shifting both break blocks by 45 min, callbacks on both queues and 20% chat deflection. This gives 55.1% overall (payments 44.8%, general 68.2%), 13.0% abandons and 82.0% for the rest of the day. Escalation is required because 55% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). Only fixing the CRM issue, or decisions above supervisor level, can close the rest of the gap.
Trade-off: P3 costs ₹540, ₹84 less than R1, and gives slightly better payments (45.6% vs 44.8%) and abandons (12.5% vs 13.0%). Overall it is lower (54.0% vs 55.1%) and general gets much less help (64.1% vs 68.2%).
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but barely moves the window (50.0%). It also lowers the rest-of-day figure to 79.2%, against 81.0% with no action.
Trade-off: P2 (₹264) reaches only 50.9%, so it does not justify its cost compared with R1.
Trade-off: R2 would reach 57.2% at the same ₹624 but breaks CX-01: the known-issue message would target refund_status on payments, which is not rising. It is excluded.
Watch: Watch payments service level and abandons from 12:45. Payments stays weakest even under R1 (44.8%). Check whether the 2 overtime agents actually accept, and track the CRM incident; if it is resolved early, handle times should fall and some actions can be stood down. Make sure the break shifts do not push rest-of-day service below about 80%.

explanations.plan: Coaching cancellation plus chat deflection for the 15:00 hour
explanations.text:
Approve P2 (cancel 15:30-16:00 coaching plus 20% chat deflection 15:00-16:00) for ₹1,491, and bring in the duty manager: it lifts 13:30-15:30 service level only to 53.1% against an 80% target.
The problem is long calls, not extra volume. Handle time on general has risen to 646 s against about 350–376 s forecast, in line with P2 incident INC-20261021-5862 (CRM customer search taking 20–40 s). Volume and staffing are close to plan. With no action, service level over 13:30-15:30 is predicted at 47.2% with 14.6% abandons. P2 raises it to 53.1% (payments 61.5%, general 43.3%) and cuts abandons to 13.0%. Rest of day improves from 79.2% to 81.2%. It is the best plan that breaks no policy rule. No plan reaches 80%, and 53% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved. The real fix is resolving the CRM incident, and they may need to push that or authorise stronger measures.
Trade-off: P0 and P1 cost nothing but leave service level at about 47% (P1 is 47.0%, so the break reshuffle and callbacks add nothing).
Trade-off: P3 costs the same ₹1,491 as P2 but predicts slightly worse: 52.6% vs 53.1%.
Trade-off: R1 and R2 predict 53.8%, with general at 47.3% and 11.9% abandons, and R2 is cheaper at ₹1,215. Both break CX-01 because the known-issue message targets refund_status on payments, which is not rising.
Trade-off: P2 mostly helps payments (61.5%). General stays weak at 43.3% because that is where the slow CRM hurts most.
Watch: Watch general handle time and the CRM incident status. If search speed recovers, handle time should fall back toward 350–376 s. If it stays near 646 s, general will stay around 43% and the duty manager should decide on further action. Also check that the chat deflection is actually taking volume from 15:00.

explanations.plan: Moderate overtime plus chat and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime for 12 general agents (11:30-15:30) plus chat deflection and IVR callback on both queues, predicted 84.1% service level for 11:00-19:45 at ₹6,804.
Calls are running about 25% above forecast on both queues with no identified cause: no incidents, no marketing sends, normal absences, and all call reasons up evenly. Doing nothing leaves the window at 72.1%, with general at 63.8%. P3 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target with no policy violations. It predicts 84.1% overall (payments 87.7%, general 80.6%) and cuts abandons from 5.9% to 3.2%. Overtime runs as two 2-hour blocks of 12 general agents. Chat deflection takes 20% of balance and payment-status enquiries, and callback runs on both queues from 11:00 to 15:00.
Trade-off: P2 (₹1,764) is ₹5,040 cheaper but just misses the target at 79.2%, and general stays at 71.4%.
Trade-off: P1 (₹900) only reaches 73.2%, barely better than no action.
Trade-off: P4 (₹11,700) gives more headroom at 87.1% and 2.7% abandons, but costs ₹4,896 more and needs 20 general plus 5 payments overtime volunteers.
Trade-off: P3 does not pull agents from payments, so the other queue is not put at risk. Payments improves to 87.7%.

explanations.plan: Outage message for card declines only + chat + more overtime (no callbacks)
explanations.text:
Approve R1: card-decline outage message, 20% chat deflection, delayed payments breaks and 40 overtime offers. Predicted 83.8% service level for 12:00-14:00 at ₹15,528.
Payments demand has surged because of P1 incident INC-20261009-3059, where the card gateway is declining debit cards. Watch: Watch overtime uptake. R1 depends on enough of the 40 payments agents accepting overtime for 12:30-14:30. Also track progress on the incident. If the gateway fix slips past 14:00, the disruption window extends beyond what this plan covers.

explanations.plan: No-cost: breaks, cross-skilled move, callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost breaks, cross-skilled move and callback lifts the disruption window to 90.6% against the 80% target
This is an outage. P1 incident INC-20261009-3059 (card authorisation gateway declining debit cards) pushed Payments calls to 212 against 108.7 forecast. Most of the excess is card_declined calls (164 vs 61.5 expected). Service level fell to 2.4% and 83 callers hung up. P1 delays breaks, moves 4 cross-skilled agents from General to Payments from 13:00 to 15:00, adds IVR callback, and plays an outage message for card_declined. For 12:45-14:45 it predicts 90.6% service level overall (Payments 95.1%, General 83.2%) and 1.6% abandons, at zero extra cost and with no policy violations. Rest of day is predicted at 92.9%.
Trade-off: No action (P0) is also predicted to reach the target at 88.5%, but P1 does better on Payments (95.1% vs 88.3%) and abandons (1.6% vs 2.1%), also at no cost.
Trade-off: General drops to 83.2% under P1, compared with 88.9% if nothing is done. That is still above target, but the other queue absorbs the move.
Trade-off: P3 performs best (95.6%, General 93.5%, 0.8% abandons) but costs INR 3,492 in overtime.
Trade-off: P2 costs INR 252 and comes in lower at 88.2%. P4 costs INR 1,620 and breaks policy MOV-03, with General predicted at 69% against the 70% floor.
Watch: Watch General service level while the 4 agents are moved; it is predicted at 83.2%, so check it stays well above the 70% floor. Also watch card_declined volume and the incident status. If the outage runs past 15:00 or volume climbs further, consider the P3 overtime.

explanations.plan: Maximum payments overtime plus deflection for the full outage
explanations.text:
Approve R1 (max payments overtime plus outage deflection, ₹4,035), and bring in the duty manager now: even the best plan only reaches about 64% against the 80% target for 13:30-15:30.
The payments spike is caused by open P1 incident INC-20261009-3059. The card authorisation gateway is failing, and card_declined calls ran at 371 against 54 expected in the last hour, so high volume will likely last until it is fixed. R1 attacks this from both sides. It offers overtime to 24 payments agents (14:00-15:00), plays IVR outage messages and deflects to chat to cut avoidable calls, and adds break delays, callbacks and cancelled payments coaching. It is predicted to lift service level from 36.7% (no action) to 63.8% over 13:30-15:30, with payments at 66.9% and general at 57.5%. Abandons are predicted to fall from 16.8% to 9.1%, and rest-of-day service level from 70.3% to 83.0%. It breaks no policy and is the best option available.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same ₹4,035 and is slightly lower overall (61.7%; payments 64.1%, general 56.9%), with near-identical abandons (9.0% vs 9.1%), so R1 gives more for the same money.
Trade-off: P3 (₹3,747, 56.1%) and P4 (₹3,648, 54.9%) save about ₹300-400 but leave service level roughly 8-9 points lower and abandons at 11.0%.
Trade-off: P2 (₹492, 40.8%) and P1 (free, 35.9%) barely improve on doing nothing. P1 also breaks policy MOV-03, with general dropping to 66% during the 15:00-16:00 move.
Trade-off: General queue under R1 is predicted at 57.5%, below the 70% escalation line, but it is still better than its 46.3% with no action.
Watch: Escalate to the duty manager: R1 is predicted at 64%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so options beyond this plan will need their decision. Track overtime uptake on the 24 offers, whether the IVR outage message and chat deflection are actually reducing payments calls, general queue service level, and the status of INC-20261009-3059. If the gateway fix runs past 15:30, the disruption window and plan will need extending.

explanations.plan: Strong combined: outage message + chat + overtime + coaching + breaks
explanations.text:
Approve P4: outage message, chat deflection, overtime for 15 payments agents, cancel coaching and delay breaks. It is the only plan that reaches the 80% target (80.5%) for 14:45-16:45, at ₹2,772.
The spike is extra demand from the UPI outage (P1 incident INC-20261010-3825), not a staffing shortfall. Payments calls hit 123 per interval against a forecast of about 70-76, and upi_payment_failed calls ran at 2.66x normal. Staffing is close to plan (26 vs 27). P4 tackles both sides. The IVR outage message and 20% chat deflection cut demand, while overtime, the cancelled 15:30 coaching and delayed breaks add capacity. Predicted service level for the window is 80.5% (payments 78.8%, general 83.8%), with abandons at 5.1%. Rest of day is predicted at 84.7%. Doing nothing leaves the window at 64.1%, with payments at 57.4% and abandons at 10.4%.
Trade-off: P2 (outage message, chat deflection and break delays) costs only ₹432 but reaches 74.5%, short of target, with payments at 71.2% and 6.6% abandons.
Trade-off: P3 (staffing only) costs more than P4 at ₹2,880 and reaches only 72.7%, because it does not reduce the outage calls.
Trade-off: P1 (no-cost break delays and callback) predicts 61.4%, slightly worse than doing nothing at 64.1%, so it is not worth using.
Trade-off: General queue is not put at risk by P4. It is predicted at 83.8%, above the 78.4% it would see with no action.
Trade-off: P4 clears the target by only 0.5 points and payments alone stays just under 80% (78.8%). There is little margin if the outage drags on or overtime uptake falls short of 15 agents.
Watch: Check overtime uptake (15 agents needed) and payments service level each interval. Monitor the UPI incident: if it extends past 16:00 the measures will need extending. If upi_payment_failed volume stays high despite the IVR message, consider escalating. No duty manager escalation is flagged for now.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): lifts the 15:30-17:30 service level to 98.5% against an 80% target, at no extra cost.
The payments spike is driven by the UPI timeout outage (P1 incident INC-20261010-3825), with upi_payment_failed calls at 4x normal. Service level has already recovered to 100% at 15:15 because staffing rose to 41 agents against 31 planned. Doing nothing is predicted to hold 94.8% over the window (payments 92.5%), so we are already above target. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It moves 8 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 16:00-17:00, delays payments breaks by 30 min, and adds IVR callback. This raises payments to 98.4% while general stays at 98.7%. Abandons fall from 1.5% to 0.4%, and rest-of-day service level improves from 92.7% to 94.8%.
Trade-off: Versus P0 (no action, INR 0): P0 already meets target at 94.8%, but payments is thinner at 92.5% and abandons are 1.5%. P1 adds headroom for no cost.
Trade-off: Versus P2 (INR 570): P2 reaches 99.8% and 0.1% abandons. It also tackles the outage directly with an IVR outage message and chat deflection. The gain is small for the spend.
Trade-off: Versus P3 (INR 3,450): P3 gives 100% and 96.6% rest of day, but uses overtime that isn't needed at current levels.
Trade-off: Risk to general: moving 8 agents leaves general at a predicted 98.7%, which is still comfortable. Delayed breaks put some extra load on payments agents.
Watch: Watch the UPI incident status and the volume of upi_payment_failed calls. If the outage drags on past 17:00 or volumes climb again, consider switching to P2 so the outage IVR message and deflection can absorb repeat status enquiries. Also check general queue service level while the 8 agents are moved.

explanations.plan: Targeted + moderate overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3: outage message, chat deflection, break delay and overtime for 25 general agents. It lifts service level to 84.3% for 11:15-13:15 at ₹5,796.
The general queue surge is driven by login_issue calls (98 vs 36.1 expected), which matches open P2 incident INC-20261024-1535, where net banking and app login are returning HTTP 503 errors. With no action, the disruption window is predicted at 48.3% service level and 12.3% abandons, with general at 27.3%. P3 tells login callers about the outage, deflects 20% of balance enquiries to chat, delays general breaks between 11:15 and 12:00, and adds 25 overtime agents from 11:45 to 13:00. That brings general to 81.8%, payments to 86.8% and abandons to 4.0%, all within policy. It is the cheapest option that reaches the 80% target.
Trade-off: P1 (no cost) and P2 (₹396) protect budget but miss the target, predicting 49.8% and 65.0%. P1 also lowers payments from 72.0% to 68.1%.
Trade-off: P4 costs ₹8,496 (₹2,700 more than P3) for only a small gain: 86.0% vs 84.3% service level and 3.1% vs 4.0% abandons.
Trade-off: P3 improves payments as well (86.8% vs 72.0% with no action), so it adds no risk to the other queue.
Trade-off: Overtime only starts at 11:45, so 11:15-11:45 will still be weak. Rest of day is predicted at 91.2%.
Watch: Check overtime uptake reaches 25 agents by 11:45. Track login_issue volume and the incident status, and stand down overtime early if the certificate fix lands. Other call reasons are also running about 1.4x normal, so re-check if general service level stays below 80% after 12:00.

explanations.plan: Targeted plus moderate overtime

explanations.plan: No-cost break shift and small move
explanations.text:
Approve P1: delay breaks by 30 minutes and move one cross-skilled agent from payments to general (14:00-15:00), at no cost.

explanations.plan: Targeted at the outage: known-issue message + chat deflection
explanations.text:
Approve P2: IVR outage message plus 20% chat deflection for payment-status and refund calls, with payments breaks delayed 45 min. Predicted 88.6% service level for 12:45-14:45 at ₹1,116.

explanations.plan: Strong with callback: P3 overtime raised moderately plus callback and break delays

Approve R2: overtime for 35 payments and 6 general agents plus callback, outage message and chat deflection lifts service level to 83.0% for 13:45-15:45 at ₹8,484.

Trade-off: The no-cost and low-cost plans (P1 ₹0, P2 ₹1,284, P4 ₹2,250) only reach 60-64%, leaving about 9-10% of callers abandoning during the outage.
Trade-off: General queue is not put at risk: R2 adds 6 general overtime agents and does not move staff off general, so general rises to 86.3% versus 74.8% with no action.
Watch: R2 depends on overtime uptake, so confirm enough of the 35 payments agents accept before 14:15. Watch the P2 incident: if the hub is not fixed by 15:45, demand will continue past the planned window and the plan will need extending. If it is fixed early, release overtime and stop the outage message.

explanations.plan: Targeted outage response + overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3: outage IVR message, chat deflection, delayed payments breaks and overtime for 30 payments agents, 13:00-15:00 (₹9,768). Best available plan, though it falls just short of the 80% target.
The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 ticket INC-20261001-6607) is driving the surge, led by card_declined calls at 2.22x normal. No plan reaches 80% over the 13:00-15:00 window, and P3 comes closest. It predicts 75.5% service level (payments 68.7%, general 87.9%) and 7.4% abandons, against 38.7% and 23.7% if we do nothing. The outage message and chat deflection cut the avoidable calls, and the overtime covers the rest. Rest of day is predicted at 89.9%. There are no policy breaches and no escalation is flagged.
Trade-off: Cost: P3 costs ₹9,768 vs ₹588 for P2 (outage response only). P2 reaches only 51.9% with 13.3% abandons.
Trade-off: R1 (₹11,976) and R2 (₹12,468) use more overtime but cost more and do slightly worse (74.8% and 73.8%), though they give general a bit more headroom (89.8% and 89.6%).
Trade-off: P4 (₹7,020) relies on staffing and callback without the outage message and only reaches 54.9%.
Trade-off: The no-cost plan P1 makes things worse (29.8%), because the callback adds load and general drops to 62.9%.
Trade-off: Risk to the other queue is low: general improves from 69.9% with no action to 87.9% under P3.
Watch: Payments is still below target at 68.7%. Check overtime uptake: the plan depends on 30 agents accepting. Also watch whether card_declined volume falls once the gateway finishes failing over to its backup site. If the outage runs past 15:00, the window will need extending.

explanations.plan: Strong recovery: full overtime plus all free levers
explanations.text:
Approve P3: full overtime plus all free levers is the only plan that reaches the 80% target (82.5%) during the 13:45-15:45 outage window, at an extra cost of ₹6,708.
Payments calls more than doubled (187 vs 88.5 forecast at 12:45) because of the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 INC-20261001-6607). Card-declined calls are 2.22x normal. Together these lift service level to 82.5% (payments 82.1%, general 83.3%) and cut abandons to 4.1%. No policy is breached, and no escalation is needed.

Trade-off: P1 costs only ₹600 but reaches just 62.0% (payments 53.8%), with 8.6% abandons.
Trade-off: Moving 3 agents out of general in P3 leaves general at 83.3%, lower than P2's 87.3% but still above target. The risk to the other queue is small.
Trade-off: Rest of day improves to 91.0% under P3, versus 79.6% with no action.
Watch: P3 depends on overtime uptake: if fewer than 30 agents accept, service level will likely fall toward P2's 76.2%. Track overtime take-up and payments service level from 14:15. Also watch the gateway failover on INC-20261001-6607; if card-declined volumes stay high past 15:45, reassess.

explanations.plan: Staffing-only: overtime plus breaks and coaching
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime for 14 payments agents plus delayed breaks and cancelled general coaching lifts service level to 80.4% for 14:30-16:30, at ₹2,895.
The payments surge is driven by the open card authorisation gateway incident (INC-20261001-6607). Card_declined calls account for about 300 of the roughly 400 extra calls. With no action, the window is predicted at 62.0% (payments 56.4%) with 8.5% abandons. P3 is the only plan that meets the 80% target at the lowest cost: it predicts 80.4% overall, payments 77.7%, general 86.7%, and 4.6% abandons. Rest of day improves to 86.8%. It follows policy.

Trade-off: P2 (outage message, chat deflection, callback) costs ₹144 but reaches only 64.6%. Its levers start late (15:45), so they do little within the window.
Trade-off: P4 adds the outage levers to P3 for ₹3,039 and lands at 80.0% (payments 77.1%), no better than P3 for ₹144 more.
Trade-off: General is not put at risk: it rises to 86.7% under P3 despite delayed breaks and cancelled coaching, because its dip looks like overflow from payments rather than a separate cause.
Watch: Payments stays below 80% on its own (77.7%) even though the overall target is met. Track how many of the 14 agents accept overtime, since a shortfall puts the target at risk. Also watch the incident status: if the gateway outage runs past 16:30 or card_declined volume keeps climbing, reassess and consider the outage IVR message.

explanations.plan: Strong+: more payments overtime + general chat deflection
explanations.text:
Approve R1: overtime on both queues, UPI outage message and chat deflection brings 11:15-13:15 service level to 85.2% for ₹9,738
Payments calls hit 220 at 11:00 against 128.7 forecast, driven by upi_payment_failed (2.2x normal, 103 excess calls). Trade-off: R1 relies on 44 agents accepting overtime and on customers taking up chat deflection. Lower uptake on either could pull payments back toward the 80% line.
Watch: Check overtime acceptance by 11:45, especially the 36 payments agents. Watch payments service level and upi_payment_failed volume each interval. Confirm the outage with IT and update the IVR message if the scope or end time changes. If the outage runs past 13:15 or payments stays below 80%, review again.

explanations.plan: Balanced: split overtime across both queues
explanations.text:
Approve P4: split overtime across payments and general plus the UPI outage message. Service level is predicted at 91.4% for 12:00–14:00, above the 80% target, for ₹6,660.

Trade-off: P2 costs only ₹1,272 but falls just short of target at 78.1% (payments 77.6%), with 5.4% abandons.
Trade-off: P1 (no-cost breaks and callbacks) is predicted at 61.7%, slightly worse than no action at 63.1%, so it does not help.
Watch: Track how many agents accept the overtime offers; P4's numbers assume 14 payments and 6 general agents take it up. Watch upi_payment_failed volume and the status of INC-20261026-6474. If the outage runs past 14:00 or call volume keeps climbing, reassess and consider involving the duty manager.

explanations.plan: Targeted login-outage response
explanations.text:
Approve P2: targeted login-outage response, predicted 83.4% service level for 14:45-16:45 at ₹450 extra.
General calls nearly doubled (124 vs 62.8 forecast at 14:30), driven mostly by login_issue calls (95 vs 39.5 expected), which points to a login or authentication failure. Watch: Check login_issue volume and general service level at each interval. Get IT to confirm or rule out a login outage, and remove the IVR message if they don't. If general stays well below 77.9% or payments falls under target, step up to P3 (overtime plus callback).

explanations.plan: No-cost: extend moves, delay breaks, keep outage message
explanations.text:
Approve P1: extend the payments-to-general moves, delay general breaks and keep the outage message, at no extra cost. Predicted service level is 96.9% for 15:30-17:30 against the 80% target.
The general queue is flooded with login_issue calls from incident INC-20261015-6270, where app and net banking login has failed since a certificate rotation. - 6 agents moved from payments to general 15:30-17:00, plus 4 more 16:00-17:00.
- General breaks from 15:30-16:15 delayed by 45 minutes.

- IVR callback on general 15:30-17:00.

Predicted results for the window are general 94.8% and payments 99.0%, with abandons at 0.2%. Rest of day is predicted at 96.1%. P1 is the cheapest plan that meets the target with no policy violations.
Trade-off: No action (P0) also meets target at 93.7%, but general is weaker at 88.8% and abandons are higher at 0.8% vs 0.2%. P1 improves customer experience for zero cost.
Trade-off: P2 adds chat deflection and cancels coaching for ₹552 and lifts general to 99.5%. The extra service is not needed to hit the target.
Trade-off: P3 adds overtime for ₹912 and reaches 99.7% overall. It costs the most, for a small gain over P1.
Trade-off: Payments is not put at risk: it holds 99.0% under P1 despite giving up up to 10 agents. Delayed breaks will put some strain on general agents.
Watch: Track login_issue volume and the incident status. If the outage runs past 17:00, extend the IVR outage message and the agent moves. If the fix lands early, release the moved agents back to payments. If general falls toward 80%, consider P2's chat deflection (₹552).

explanations.plan: Compliant recovery with stronger internal support
explanations.text:
Approve R2: overtime on both queues, callbacks, chat deflection and internal moves lift service level to 81.5% for 13:45-17:15 at ₹14,607 extra cost.
The problem is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit upgrade SMS (MKT-2026-951) has pushed general queue calls up 72%, and new_offer_enquiry is running at 5.2x normal. Overtime on payments, callbacks, delayed breaks and cancelled payments coaching keep payments healthy even after 9 cross-skilled agents move to general from 16:00. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 85.2%.
Trade-off: Cost: R2 is ₹825 more than R1 (₹13,782). R1 is also compliant but falls just short of target at 79.6%, with general at 77.1%.
Trade-off: Cheaper options don't recover service: no action gives 59.9% (general 47.6%), and P1 (₹750) actually drops to 57.9%.
Trade-off: P2 and P3 use an IVR outage message without a confirmed incident, which breaks policy CX-01. P3 also only reaches 76.6% despite costing ₹10,362.
Trade-off: Risk to payments: R2 pulls the most agents from payments (9 at 16:00-17:00) and cancels payments coaching. It relies on 10 payments agents accepting overtime to keep payments at 84.9%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: general callbacks run until 16:00, so some customers wait for a call back rather than being answered live.
Watch: Watch how many agents take the overtime offer (28 + 8 on general, 10 on payments); a low uptake is the main risk to hitting target. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against the 5.2x trend and check general service level is recovering toward 78.6%. Check payments service level when the 9 agents move across at 16:00. No escalation is needed.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): predicted 84.2% service level for 14:30-19:15 against the 80% target, at no extra cost.
The problem is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit upgrade SMS (MKT-2026-951) pushed general queue calls to +72% by 13:30, mostly new_offer_enquiry calls at 5.2x normal. Staffing is only about 2 agents below plan. P1 meets the target without spending anything. It delays general breaks 15:00-16:00 by 45 minutes, moves 5 cross-skilled agents from payments to general 17:00-18:00 and 2 agents 19:00-20:00, and offers IVR callback on general 16:00-18:00. Predicted abandons fall to 2.9% (3.3% with no action). Rest of day is 84.3%. The plan follows policy, and no escalation is needed.

Trade-off: P4 gives 88.5% combined and 83.6% on general with no customer-facing changes and no policy issues. It costs INR 2,160 in overtime. Keep it as the fallback if P1 underdelivers.
Trade-off: P2 (86.7%, INR 120) and P3 (91.1%, INR 2,160) break policy CX-01. A known-issue IVR message needs a confirmed outage or incident, and there isn't one, so neither can be used as is.
Watch: Watch new_offer_enquiry volume and general queue service level, especially 15:00-16:00 while breaks are delayed and 17:00-18:00. If general stays well below 78% or abandons go above 3%, switch to the P4 overtime offers.

explanations.plan: Staffing-first: overtime, moves and chat, no IVR message
explanations.text:
Approve P4: overtime, cross-skilled moves and chat deflection. Predicted 86.2% service level over 15:15-19:45 for ₹4,092.
The spike is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit SMS (MKT-2026-951) drove new_offer_enquiry calls to 5.2x normal, and general queue service level has fallen to 0% with 28 abandons. It predicts 86.2% overall, with general at 79.2% and payments at 95.1%. Abandons fall to 2.6% from 5.0%, and the rest of the day is predicted at 86.4%.

Watch: Check how many agents accept overtime, especially the 12 needed for 17:00-19:00. P4 depends on it. Track the general queue closely, since it is predicted just under 80%. Escalation is not required.

explanations.plan: Full response with overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3: full response with overtime. It is the only plan that reaches the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹15,840.
Payments calls are running up to 72% above forecast (112 vs 65 at 09:15). The rise most likely comes from the 08:35 UPI cashback push, MKT-2026-409, sent to 1.2M app users. Predicted results: 91.1% service level (payments 92.2%, general 89.4%), 2.5% abandons, and 93.7% for the rest of the day. It has no policy violations.

Trade-off: P2 costs only ₹2,880 but falls short at 71.4% (payments 64.7%). It is the fallback if overtime take-up is poor.
Trade-off: P4 costs more than P3 (₹16,524) and only reaches 77.4%, because it drops the IVR message and callback. Its one advantage is less friction for customers in the IVR.
Trade-off: P3 means customers hear an IVR message and are pushed towards chat and callbacks. The general queue improves under P3 (89.4% vs 75.2% with no action), so there is no risk to it.
Trade-off: There is no escalation flag, but ₹15,840 is the largest spend that meets the target.
Watch: Check overtime acceptance by 10:00. If fewer agents accept than offered, the result moves towards P2's 71%. Track payments volume against the 112-per-interval peak, and check whether refund_status, upi_payment_failed and payment_status_enquiry calls ease off. If they don't, the campaign link may be wrong and the volume could persist past 14:15.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): lifts the 14:00–17:15 window to 80.8%, just over the 80% target, at zero extra cost, but payments stays below target at 76.6%.
The payments surge looks driven by the 08:35 UPI cashback push (MKT-2026-409), with calls up to +72% at 09:15 and service level down to 49%. Confidence is medium because the 08:00 bump came before the push. Doing nothing predicts 79.9% for the window, just under target. P1 delays payments breaks 14:00–15:00 by 45 minutes, runs IVR callback on payments 14:00–16:00, and moves 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:00–16:00. That gives 80.8% overall and cuts abandons from 5.2% to 4.8%, with no extra cost and no policy issues. General still improves slightly, from 87.2% to 88.0%. The rest of the day is predicted at 86.6%.

Trade-off: P4 (₹1,080) reaches 83.8% overall but only 78.9% on payments. It also delays breaks on both queues, which touches general staff unnecessarily.
Trade-off: P1 moves 4 agents out of general for an hour. General is still predicted at 88.0%, so the risk to that queue is low.
Watch: Track payments service level and abandons from 14:00. The margin over 80% is only 0.8 points, so if payments volume runs above forecast (for example, a second campaign push), be ready to step up to P2's chat deflection on refund_status and payment_status_enquiry. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Strongest: all levers plus remaining overtime budget
explanations.text:
Approve P3: all levers plus overtime lifts the 14:45–18:45 service level to 81.2%, the only plan that reaches the 80% target, for ₹5,784.

Also watch whether payments volume keeps climbing beyond the campaign estimate; if it does, there is no overtime left and the duty manager may need to be involved.

explanations.plan: No-cost: lend payments agents to general and add callback for the 19:00 hour
explanations.text:
Approve P1: lend 2 cross-skilled payments agents to general and switch on IVR callback for general, 19:00–20:00. No extra cost.
Agents on general dropped suddenly at 17:00 to 25 against 32 planned, then 23 against 32 at 17:15. The attendance log doesn't explain it: 3 sick calls against a usual 2.4, the last logged at 14:57. explanations.plan: Maximum compliant overtime with free support levers

Approve R1: maximum compliant overtime plus free levers. It is the best available plan, but it still falls short of the 80% target (73.8% predicted for 12:30–15:30).
Two problems are hitting at once. The FD special-rate email (MKT-2026-556) has pushed general calls 20–45% over forecast, with new_offer_enquiry at 2.74x normal. Trade-off: P2 and P3 use an IVR known-issue message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage. P3 would also only reach 68.3%.
Trade-off: No-cost levers alone (P1) barely help: 41.6% for ₹675.
Watch: Overtime uptake is the main risk. The 73.8% assumes 53 agents accept the offers, so confirm acceptances quickly, especially the 35 general agents for 13:00. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against forecast in case the campaign response keeps growing. Also check that the payments sick-call gap doesn't widen.

explanations.plan: No-cost: breaks, a short loan from general, payments callback

Approve P1: no-cost break delay, a short 2-agent loan from general, and payments callback. It is predicted to hold 91.2% service level for 13:15-15:15 at zero extra cost.

Trade-off: P0 (no action) is also free and predicted at 91.0% with a slightly lower abandon rate (2.2% vs 2.5%). P1 adds only 0.2 points, but it actively supports the short-staffed payments queue.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:

For 17:00–18:00 it moves 2 agents from payments back to general. Predicted results: payments 92.3%, general 91.4%, abandon rate 1.9% (vs 2.3% with no action), rest of day 92.7%. Also check that the delayed payments breaks are taken and that the 17:00 move back to general happens.

explanations.plan: Overtime pushed to the budget limit + chat on both queues, no general callback

Approve R1: overtime for 8 general agents, chat deflection on both queues and 2 agents lent from payments. Predicted 80.7% service level for 18:15-20:00 at ₹1,260.

If too few of the 8 agents accept overtime, or chat uptake falls below 20%, general will stay well short of target and the plan is unlikely to reach 80% overall. Also watch payments between 18:15 and 19:00 while the 2 agents are lent out. Bring them back early if payments drops toward its current 25% level.

explanations.plan: Front-loaded overtime with break shift, deflection on both queues
explanations.text:
Approve R2: front-loaded general overtime, a short break delay and chat deflection on both queues lift service level to 80.4% for 11:45-15:30, just above the 80% target, for ₹18,441.

No escalation is needed.

explanations.plan: Staffing-only with remaining overtime budget
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime for 12 general agents plus break delay and cross-skill moves, lifting service level to 88.0% (target 80%) for ₹3,600.
A 10:50 regional TV ad for the zero-balance savings account pushed general calls to 122–124 per interval against about 79 forecast. New-offer enquiries are at 3.7x normal. P3 offers overtime to 12 general agents from 13:30 to 15:30. It also delays general breaks 13:00–14:00 by 45 minutes and moves cross-skilled agents between queues. Predicted results for the window are 88.0% overall, general 81.9%, payments 95.1% and abandons 2.3%. It is the only policy-compliant plan that reaches target. Rest of day rises to 91.2%.

explanations.plan: Earlier overtime and wider chat deflection, without break delays or callback
explanations.text:
Approve R1: earlier overtime plus wider chat deflection. It gives the best recovery available (75.7% vs 80% target) for ₹9,762, but it still falls short of target.
Payments calls jumped to +52% above forecast after the 10:55 reward-points email, and service level fell to 32%. Doing nothing leaves the 11:45-15:15 window at 40.4% (Payments 29.3%) with 15.7% abandons. No plan reaches 80% over the window. R1 comes closest at 75.7% (Payments 73.3%, General 79.8%) and cuts abandons to 6.2%. It does this by starting overtime at 11:45 (35 agents to 13:45, then 22 to 15:15) and deflecting 20% of refund-status, payment-status and new-offer enquiries to chat. Rest-of-day service level reaches 85.4%.
Trade-off: Cost: ₹9,762, the most expensive option along with R2. That is ₹300 more than P4 (67.4%) and ₹2,400 more than P3 (63.0%), for 8-13 points more service level.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same but does worse (73.0% overall, General 76.2%) because it pulls 5 agents from General at 15:00 rather than 3.
Trade-off: Risk to General: R1 still moves 3 cross-skilled agents to Payments from 15:00 to 16:00, but General is predicted at 79.8%, better than with no action (61.5%).
Trade-off: Customer impact: R1 drops IVR callback and break delays. Chat deflection steers some callers to chat. Payments coaching from 15:30 to 16:00 is cancelled.
Trade-off: The no-cost options (P1 37.4%, P2 42.0%) barely move service level, and P1 is worse than doing nothing.
Watch: R1 depends on enough agents accepting the overtime from 11:45. If take-up is low, service level will stay well below 75.7%. Confirm the reward-email calls really are Payments demand (the diagnosis confidence is medium), and check whether the surge eases after 12:00. Keep an eye on General after 15:00 when the 3 agents move across.

explanations.plan: Strongest: overtime, moves, break shift and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime, callback, cross-skilled moves and a break shift. It is the best available plan, lifting service level to 74.3% for 12:30-16:00, but still short of the 80% target.
Payments calls jumped after the 10:55 reward-points email to 500,000 card holders. They reached +52% at 11:30 (164 vs 108 expected) and service level fell to 32%. With no action, the 12:30-16:00 window is predicted at 64.9% (Payments 56.4%) with 8.5% abandons. P3 offers overtime to 9 Payments agents 13:00-15:00 and runs IVR callback on Payments 12:30-15:30. The campaign link is medium confidence: the timing and audience fit, but the email is about card rewards rather than payments.
Trade-off: P2 costs the same ₹2,160 but reaches only 70.9% (Payments 64.0%) with 6.2% abandons. P3 adds the free moves and break shift on top of it.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but reaches only 67.1% (Payments 60.2%) and pulls General down to 83.0%.
Trade-off: R1 also costs ₹2,160 and moves more General agents, but scores slightly lower overall at 73.9%, with General at 85.1%.
Trade-off: R2 costs ₹2,835 and cancels General coaching for 74.2%, which is no better than P3.
Trade-off: General stays healthy under P3 at 86.7%, so the agent moves carry little risk to that queue.
Watch: Check Payments volume against forecast every 15 minutes. If calls keep climbing past +52%, or General drops toward 80% once the moves start at 14:00, re-plan. Confirm overtime uptake from the 9 agents before 13:00.

explanations.plan: Strongest without overtime: moves, chat deflection and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P4: move cross-skilled agents, cancel payments coaching, add chat deflection and IVR callback. Predicted 77.2% service level for 16:15-20:00, short of the 80% target, at ₹1,347 extra.
Payments demand jumped after the 10:55 reward-points email to 500,000 card holders. Calls reached +52% at 11:30 (164 vs 108 expected) and service level fell to 32%. The extra calls are mostly generic reasons: other_payments (1.77x normal) and refund_status (1.56x). Confidence in the cause is medium, because the email is about card rewards rather than clearly Payments & UPI. With no action, service level over 16:15-20:00 is predicted at 69.3%, with payments at 59.5%. P4 is the best plan that stays within policy. It lifts service level to 77.2% (payments 71.7%) and cuts abandons from 9.3% to 6.4%. No compliant plan reaches 80%.
Trade-off: Cost: P4 costs ₹1,347, the same as P3 and R1, and gives the best result of the three. P3 reaches 76.4%, R1 only 75.1% despite its bigger agent moves. The cheaper staffing-only options (P1, P2: ₹75) barely help, at 70.2% and 69.5%.
Trade-off: General queue: moving agents drops general from 94.4% to 90.2%, still comfortably healthy. R1's larger moves push general down to 88.8% and do worse overall.
Trade-off: Customer impact: chat deflection and callbacks steer some refund/payment-status callers away from waiting on the phone line, which helps cut abandons to 6.4%.
Trade-off: R2 would reach 85.3%, but its known-issue IVR message breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident, so it is not recommended.
Watch: Payments will still be below the 80% target, so keep an eye on payments service level and abandons, especially in the 17:00-18:00 peak when 6 agents are moved. Check that general stays near 90%. If the extra calls turn out not to be about Payments & UPI, re-check the plan.

explanations.plan: Targeted demand: chat deflection for rising reasons plus callback
explanations.text:
Approve P2: chat deflection plus callback lifts the 12:45-19:45 window to 83.4% service level for ₹1,296
Payments calls are running about 24.5% above forecast (1524 vs 1224.5 today) with no outage, incident or campaign to explain it, and every call reason is up. With no action the window is predicted at 78.1% (payments 72.4%), below the 80% target. P2 deflects 20% of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls to chat over the two pressure periods (12:45-15:00 and 18:00-20:00), adds IVR callback 13:00-15:00 and delays payments breaks by 45 minutes. This brings the window to 83.4% overall and cuts abandons from 5.3% to 4.3%. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches target. Escalation is not required.
Trade-off: P1 (₹750) is cheaper but makes things worse: 76.7% overall, 70.1% on payments, 5.9% abandons.
Trade-off: P3 (₹6,480, 87.6%) and P4 (₹5,616, 91.3%, payments 90.0%) give more headroom but cost roughly 4-5x more and depend on agents accepting overtime.
Trade-off: Payments itself is predicted at 79.3% under P2, just under 80%. The overall target is met because general holds at 90.7%. P2 moves no agents off general, so there is no risk to that queue.
Trade-off: Chat deflection asks some customers to switch channels, so chat volumes will rise during the deflection windows.
Watch: Check payments service level and chat backlog through 13:00-15:00. If the surge keeps growing, or payments stays well below 80%, be ready to add overtime as in P4. Payments has the least margin of the two queues.

explanations.plan: Overtime-backed recovery
explanations.text:
Approve P3 (overtime-backed recovery): the only option that reaches the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹5,496
Payments calls have run 21-44% above forecast since 11:00 (824 calls vs 634.5 forecast over the last 8 intervals), and service level fell to 15.4% at 12:45. The rise is spread evenly across all call reasons and has no clear cause, so we should plan for it to continue. P3 offers overtime to 18 payments agents 13:30-15:30 and 5 agents 19:00-20:00. It adds chat deflection, delayed breaks and a move of 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:00-16:00. For the disruption window (13:00-19:15) it predicts 86.1% service level: payments 83.8% and general 90.5%. Predicted abandons are 3.0% and rest of day is 85.7%. There are no policy violations.
Trade-off: Cost: P3 adds ₹5,496. P2 costs ₹1,266 but reaches only 76.6% (payments 71.2%), missing the 80% target. P1 and no action cost nothing but predict 72.7% and 73.6%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: predicted abandons are 3.0% under P3, against 5.6% (P2), 6.5% (P1) and 7.4% (no action).
Trade-off: General queue: moving 4 agents does not hurt general under P3, which is predicted at 90.5% against 89.5% with no action. P1 and P2 do pull general down slightly, to 87.6% and 86.9%.
Trade-off: Risk: the plan relies on enough agents accepting the overtime offers. If too few accept, results will fall toward P2's level.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 13:30 and payments call volume against forecast each interval. If volume keeps rising past the +44% peak, or acceptance is low, reassess and consider involving the duty manager.

explanations.plan: No-cost: shift late-morning breaks plus callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: shift late-morning breaks by 45 minutes and switch on IVR callback, at no extra cost, for a predicted 91.0% service level from 10:00 to 12:00 against an 80% target.
General calls are running 26% above forecast for the day so far, and service level fell to 44.1% at 09:45 with 6 abandons. Every call reason rose by a similar amount, and no marketing send, incident or absence explains it, so we can't tell how long it will last. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just clear target at 83.6%, with payments at 82.3%, which leaves little margin if the surge grows. P1 also costs nothing and lifts the window to 91.0% (payments 88.7%, general 94.2%). It cuts predicted abandons from 3.5% to 2.1% and needs no policy exceptions.
Trade-off: Against P0 (no action, ₹0): same cost, but P0 runs close to target, especially on payments. P1 adds a buffer. The cost is that delayed breaks and callbacks shift some load later, so the rest-of-day forecast dips slightly from 92.6% to 92.3%.
Trade-off: Against P2 (chat deflection, ₹276): slightly better at 91.7% with 1.7% abandons, but it costs money for a small gain. It also targets balance enquiries when no single topic is driving the surge.
Trade-off: Against P3 (₹2,436) and P4 (₹5,760): overtime pushes the window to 95.9–96.3% with abandons of 1.0% or less, well above what the target needs. P4 is the hedge if the surge proves to be lasting.
Trade-off: Customer impact: callers on general from 10:00 and on payments from 11:00 will be offered a callback instead of waiting, and agents take their 11:00 breaks 45 minutes later.
Watch: No escalation is needed. Because the cause is unknown, check general volume against forecast at around 10:30 and 11:00. If it keeps climbing or payments service level drops toward 80%, consider moving to the overtime options (P3, or P4 if the surge looks set to run past midday).

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost rebalance. Delay the 12:30-13:00 breaks by 30 minutes and swap 2 cross-skilled agents between queues later. This is predicted to give 95.8% service level for 12:30-14:30, against an 80% target.
Since 12:00, agents on the phones have fallen below plan in both queues. Payments had 24 and then 23 against 31 and 29 planned. General had 24 and then 21 against 27 planned. Service level dropped to 19.6% and 47.4% in payments and 24.7% and 11.7% in general. The attendance feed shows no absences and no incident explains the gap, so the cause is unknown. Check for off-plan breaks or meetings, or a phone or login problem. General volume is also 26.6% over forecast. P1 costs nothing and breaks no policy. It is predicted to reach 96.4% in payments and 95.1% in general over the window, with 1.2% abandons and 96.6% for the rest of the day.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) is also predicted to meet target at 92.8%, but P1 adds margin at no cost. That margin matters while the cause of the drop is unknown.
Trade-off: P3 (chat deflection) is slightly stronger at 96.5% with 0.8% abandons, but costs INR 336 and pushes some customers to chat.
Trade-off: P2 (callbacks) costs nothing but predicts only 92.8%, with higher abandons at 1.6% and general at 92.0%.
Trade-off: P4 (overtime) costs INR 360 for 92.8%, no better than doing nothing in the window.
Trade-off: P1's agent moves take cover from one queue to help the other. General is still predicted at 95.1%, so the risk to it looks low.
Watch: Confirm agents actually come back on the phones and find why staffing dropped. These predictions assume staffing recovers. If agent counts stay below plan, or general volume keeps running about 27% over forecast and service level slips toward 80%, reconsider P3.

explanations.plan: Demand-side: chat deflection, callbacks and lighter overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P4: chat deflection, callbacks and lighter overtime on General lifts service level to 80.5% for 09:00-15:30, meeting the 80% target at the lowest cost (₹5,892).
General is short because of a sick wave, not because of extra calls. There are 9 sick absences against a usual 2.4, leaving 16 agents on the phones against 20 planned. Calls are actually 15% below forecast. With no action, service level over 09:00-15:30 is predicted at 68.0% (General 61.1%), with 7.4% abandons. P4 is predicted to reach 80.5% overall (Payments 84.7%, General 75.3%) and cut abandons to 4.2%. It does this by moving 20% of simple enquiries to chat on both queues, offering callbacks, delaying General breaks, and adding 6 overtime agents on General from 11:00 to 15:00. It is the cheapest plan that hits target with no policy violations. Rest of day is predicted at 86.7%.
Trade-off: P3 (overtime on both queues) predicts 81.3%, with General at 77.3% and abandons at 3.8%. It is slightly stronger but costs ₹11,415, nearly double P4.
Trade-off: P2 (General overtime only) costs ₹7,815, more than P4, yet just misses target at 79.0%.
Trade-off: P1 (no-cost moves, ₹75) does not help: it predicts 66.9%, slightly worse than doing nothing (68.0%).
Trade-off: Under P4, General stays weakest at 75.3%. Results also depend on customers actually taking up chat and callbacks.
Watch: Payments also has 7 sick absences against a usual 2.6, so the illness may be spreading. If more Payments or General agents drop out, or chat uptake is low, General could fall further below 80%. In that case, be ready to step up to P3's overtime on both queues and involve the duty manager.

explanations.plan: Balanced: break shifting plus moderate overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3: delay the late-morning breaks and offer moderate overtime on both queues. This is predicted to lift service level to 83.5% for 10:45-15:30, at an extra cost of ₹5,400.
General is short-staffed because of illness, not because of call volume. It has 9 sick absences against about 2.4 on a usual day, and 16 agents have been on the phones since 08:30 against 20 planned. If we do nothing, service level is predicted to fall to 79.1% over the disruption window, just under the 80% target, with General at 74.2%. P3 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It brings General to 81.3%, Payments to 85.1% and the overall figure to 83.5%. Predicted abandons drop from 4.3% to 3.4%, and the rest-of-day service level rises to 88.5%.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) costs nothing but misses the target at 79.1%, with General at 74.2% and 4.3% abandons.
Trade-off: P1 (break shifting only) costs nothing but makes things worse: 76.8% overall, General at 72.1% and abandons up to 5.7%.
Trade-off: P2 (heavier overtime) gives a much safer margin at 90.0%, with General at 86.9% and 1.9% abandons. It costs ₹8,550, which is ₹3,150 more than P3.

Watch: Check how many agents accept the overtime and whether more sick calls come in on either queue. If General falls below 80% or Payments absences keep rising, consider moving to P2. No escalation is needed for now.

explanations.plan: Sick-wave backfill with overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime backfill for the General sick wave, predicted 84.6% service level for 11:45-15:30 at ₹6,870 extra.
General has 9 sick absences against about 2.4 on a usual day, leaving 16 agents on the phones against 20 planned since 08:30. Trade-off: Customer impact: P3 has the lowest predicted abandon rate at 3.3%. The others range from 4.6% (P2) to 6.2% (P1). P1 is worse than doing nothing.

Further absences there could pull Payments below target, particularly while its 2 cross-skilled agents are on General.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost rebalance lifts service level to 88.8% for 13:15-15:30 against the 80% target
A sick wave has removed staff on both queues: 8 payments and 12 general agents are off sick against usual levels of 2.6 and 2.4, and payments had 26 agents on at 13:00 versus 34 planned. Call volume is below forecast (payments -2.7%, general -7.6%), so this is a staffing gap, not a demand spike. Doing nothing is predicted to reach 84.8%, but payments would sit at 81.0%, only just above target. P1 delays payments breaks 13:15-14:15 by 30 minutes and moves 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 13:15-14:00. It also moves 2 back from payments to general 19:00-20:00. This lifts payments to 85.2% and general to 93.6%, and cuts abandons from 3.0% to 1.8%. It costs nothing and breaks no policy.

Trade-off: P0 costs nothing but leaves payments at 81.0% with 3.0% abandons, a thin margin if more sickness is reported.
