Watch: Check for any further sick calls on payments. P1's payments margin is 85.2% against an 80% target, so if more agents drop out, move to the overtime option (P3, INR 720). Make sure the delayed breaks are actually taken once the 13:15-14:15 window ends.

explanations.plan: No-cost: shift breaks, callback and a late cross-skill move
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost break shift, IVR callbacks and one late cross-skill move, predicted 94.5% service level for 15:00-20:00 at no extra cost.
A sick wave (12 absences on payments vs a usual 2.6, 13 on general vs 2.4) has cut staffing, pushing service level down to 56.8% on payments and 72.4% on general at 13:30. For the 15:00-20:00 window, even doing nothing is predicted to reach 93.7%, above the 80% target. P1 nudges that to 94.5% (payments 93.8%, general 95.4%) and cuts predicted abandons from 1.6% to 1.3%, at zero cost and with no policy issues. It does this by delaying payments breaks by 30 min, offering IVR callback on payments 15:00-16:00 and 18:00-19:30 and on general 18:00-19:00, and moving 1 cross-skilled agent from general to payments 19:00-20:00. No escalation is needed.
Trade-off: P2 reaches 95.9% with 1.1% abandons but costs INR 858. It cancels payments coaching and pushes 20% of some enquiries to chat, which affects customers.
Trade-off: P3 reaches 95.4% with 1.1% abandons for INR 720 of evening overtime on 3 payments agents.
Trade-off: P1 relies on callbacks, so some customers wait for a call back rather than being answered live.
Trade-off: P1 moves 1 agent off general 19:00-20:00, but general is still predicted at 95.4%, the same as with no action.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) already meets the target at 93.7%, so P1 is a low-risk improvement rather than a rescue.
Watch: Check payments service level and the callback backlog around 15:30 and again at 18:00. Further fever absences could widen the gap beyond these predictions; if payments heads toward 80%, consider P3's overtime.

explanations.plan: No-cost: cross-skilled moves plus callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: move 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments (09:00-14:00) and switch on IVR callback for payments (09:00-15:00), at no extra cost.
This morning's problem is staffing, not demand. Payments had 7 flu sick calls against a usual 2 per day, leaving 13 agents on the phones against 18 planned. Volume is only 5.4% over forecast, and handle time is close to plan. P1 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the 09:00-15:00 window, at a predicted 80.1% overall. Abandons are predicted to fall to 5.1%, against 78.3% service level and 5.5% abandons if we do nothing. It costs INR 0 and breaks no policy. General is not hurt: it actually edges up from 89.5% to 89.9%.
Trade-off: Payments itself stays weak at 72.8% under P1. The plan meets target only on the combined figure, so payments callers still wait longer than standard.
Trade-off: The 80.1% prediction gives almost no margin over the 80% target. If more absences come in or volume rises further, P1 could fall short.
Trade-off: P2 costs INR 1,056 and lifts payments to 77.7% (83.1% overall, 4.1% abandons). It relies on deflecting 20% of payment status calls to chat and on moving 3 agents out of general until 11:00.
Trade-off: P3 costs INR 4,500 and adds overtime, reaching 84.1% overall with payments at 78.9%. P4 costs INR 8,280, takes no one from general, and gives the strongest result: 89.4% overall, payments 86.1%, 2.4% abandons.
Watch: Watch payments service level and abandons after 09:00, and any further sick calls. If payments is not recovering toward the low 70s by mid-morning, or the overall figure dips below 80%, move to P2. P2 is the cheap step up, and overtime (P3/P4) is the fallback. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Heavier payments overtime plus wider deflection
explanations.text:
Approve R2: heavier payments overtime plus wider chat deflection. It is predicted to lift service level to 81.0% over 09:45-15:15 for ₹10,782, the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target.
This is a staffing problem, not a demand problem. Payments had 7 flu sick calls this morning against a usual 2.0 a day, leaving 13 agents on the phones against 18 planned. Volume is only 5.4% over forecast and handle time is close to plan, so the fix has to add capacity or take calls away. With no action, service level is predicted at 53.0% for the disruption window (payments 39.2%), with 11.8% of callers abandoning. R2 does both: it moves 2 cross-skilled agents across for 10:00-11:00, delays payments breaks by 45 minutes, offers overtime to 18 payments agents through 15:00, and deflects 20% of status, refund and balance enquiries to chat. The predicted result is 81.0% overall (payments 76.3%, general 87.2%), abandons down to 4.5%, and 87.6% for the rest of the day. There are no policy violations.
Trade-off: Cost vs R1: R1 reaches a slightly higher 83.1% (general 91.3%, abandons 4.1%) but costs ₹11,322, which is ₹540 more than R2.
Trade-off: Cost vs P4: P4 is ₹1,704 cheaper at ₹9,078 but is predicted to fall just short of target at 79.0%.
Trade-off: The cheaper plans miss the target by a wide margin. P2 (₹6,468) is predicted at 76.0% and P3 (₹6,750) at 71.6%, and the no-cost rebalance P1 reaches only 56.1%.
Trade-off: Risk to the other queue: general should still improve on doing nothing, rising from 71.8% to 87.2%, even though it lends 2 agents for an hour. Payments remains below 80% on its own at 76.3%, so customers on that queue will still feel some impact.
Watch: The 81.0% forecast depends on most of the 18 overtime offers being accepted, so confirm the take-up early. R2 clears the target by only 1 point, and fewer acceptances could push it below 80%. Also check that the chat deflection is actually moving status and refund enquiries off the phones. Watch for further flu absences in payments, since more sick calls would widen the gap.

explanations.plan: No-cost: move agents, delay breaks, extend callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost rebalancing keeps both queues above the 80% target through 12:45–15:30
Payments lost capacity to a flu-driven sick wave (11 absences vs a usual 2; agents fell from 36 to 24, below the 28–29 planned), and service level dipped to 60.3% at 12:30. Demand is only modestly up (+6%), so this is a capacity gap. The model predicts the disruption window recovers even with no action (85.7%), but P1 adds a margin at zero cost. It moves 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 13:00–14:00, delays payments breaks 13:45–14:30 by 45 minutes and runs IVR callback on payments 15:00–16:00. Predicted service level is 87.0% overall (payments 87.9%, general 85.9%), abandon rate falls to 2.8% from 3.6%, and rest of day is 92.7%. No policy issues; no escalation needed.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) also meets target at 85.7% for ₹0, but abandons are higher (3.6% vs 2.8%) and payments has less buffer if more sickness is logged.
Trade-off: P2, P3 and P4 push payments to 92–95% and cut abandons to 2.0–2.4%, but cost ₹1,815–2,535 in overtime for a target P1 already meets for free.
Trade-off: General is not hurt by lending 2 agents in P1: its predicted service level is 85.9% vs 85.4% with no action.
Trade-off: Delayed breaks put some extra load on payments agents, who are already short-staffed.
Watch: Watch payments agent count and service level each interval from 13:00. If more absences arrive or payments drops back toward 80%, switch to P4 (₹1,815, payments 92.4%), the cheapest overtime option. Also check general stays above 80% while its 2 agents are on payments.

explanations.plan: No-cost: breaks, cross-skill moves, callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost breaks, cross-skill moves and callback keep Payments on target at zero extra cost
The Payments shortfall is a capacity problem, not a demand problem. There have been 11 sick absences today against a usual 2, mostly flu. Agents on the phones fell to 24 against 28–29 planned, and service level dropped to 60.3% at 12:30. Volume is only up 6%. For the disruption window (15:00–18:45), the forecast now looks healthy even with no action: P0 predicts 97.3%, well above the 80% target. P1 nudges that to 97.5% (Payments 96.4%, General 99.1%) at no cost. It also cuts predicted abandons from 0.7% to 0.3% and lifts the rest-of-day figure to 95.0%. It does this by moving 3 cross-skilled agents to Payments 15:00–16:00, delaying 15:00–15:45 breaks by 30 minutes, moving 2 more agents 18:00–20:00 and switching on IVR callback 18:00–20:00. No policy issues; no escalation needed.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) also meets target at 97.3% and costs nothing, but abandons stay at 0.7% versus 0.3% with P1.
Trade-off: P2 costs ₹759 for 97.6% (Payments 96.7%). It slightly dents General (98.9% vs 99.1%) and keeps abandons at 0.7%, so it is a marginal gain for real money.
Trade-off: P3 costs ₹1,440 for the best result, 97.9% (Payments 97.0%, rest of day 96.2%). That is only 0.4 points better than P1 in the window.
Trade-off: P1 takes 3 and then 2 agents from General, but General is still predicted at 99.1%, so risk to that queue looks low.
Trade-off: Delaying breaks asks more of an already short-staffed Payments team.
Watch: Watch Payments agents on the phones and service level through 15:00–16:00 and again from 18:00. Any further flu absences could widen the gap beyond what the free levers cover. If Payments drifts toward 80%, P3's evening overtime (₹1,440) is the ready step-up. Also confirm that General holds near 99% while it lends agents.

explanations.plan: Deflection and overtime on both queues, no callbacks
explanations.text:
Approve R1: deflection plus overtime on both queues lifts service level to 82% (target 80%) for 08:15-15:30 at ₹16,122.
General has 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4. It is down to 51 agents against 57.6 expected, and demand and handle time are on plan. Doing nothing is predicted to give 55.4% over the disruption window (general 45.8%) with 10.8% abandons. R1 is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches the 80% target. It uses 20% chat deflection on both queues, cancels all coaching 09:00-12:00, offers overtime to 10 general agents 09:00-15:00 and offers overtime to 6 payments agents 11:00-15:00.
Trade-off: P4 (₹11,802) and P2 (₹12,258) are about ₹4,000 cheaper but fall short at 77.5% and 76.0%. General would stay below target at 77.0% and 74.0%.
Trade-off: R2 reaches 85.0% with general at 82.8% and 2.9% abandons, but costs ₹18,372, about ₹2,250 more than R1.
Trade-off: P1 adds no overtime (₹450) and actually predicts slightly worse than doing nothing, at 54.2%.
Trade-off: General is only just over target at 80.2%, so R1 has little margin if overtime take-up is short.
Watch: Check overtime acceptance on general first. R1 needs all 10 agents in each block to hold general above 80%. Also watch payments absence: it is 6 against a usual 2.6, which could put its cover at risk. Re-check once more intervals of data arrive, because only one interval has been seen so far.

explanations.plan: No-cost: shift current breaks and add callbacks
explanations.text:
Approve P1: shift the 09:45-10:15 breaks by 30 minutes and add IVR callbacks on both queues, at no extra cost, holding a predicted 85.7% service level against the 80% target.
General is short because of a sick wave: 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4, leaving 51 agents against 57.6 expected. Demand and handle time are close to plan, so this is a staffing problem, not a volume one. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and meets the target over the 09:45-15:30 window. It predicts 84.2% on general and 86.9% on payments, with abandons at 3.0%. Doing nothing (P0) would also just clear the target at 85.6%, so P1 is a small, free safety margin rather than a rescue. The prediction rests on only one interval of data so far.
Trade-off: P1 vs P0: both cost nothing. P1 lifts general from 83.8% to 84.2% and cuts abandons from 3.2% to 3.0%. Rest-of-day service level dips slightly, from 90.1% to 89.9%, because the breaks are pushed later.
Trade-off: P2 (INR 4,320) uses overtime on general. It raises the window to 89.7% (general 91.3%) and cuts abandons to 2.2%, giving much more headroom if absences keep rising.
Trade-off: P3 (INR 4,680) adds overtime on payments as well. It reaches 90.5% overall and 91.0% on payments, and is the best protection if payments' high absence (6 against a usual 2.6) starts to bite.
Trade-off: P1 changes nothing on payments' service level (86.9%, same as no action), so payments has no extra cover if its absences worsen.
Watch: General's service level in the next few intervals: the margin over 80% is only about 4 points. Also watch payments absence and service level. If either queue trends toward 80%, move to P2, or to P3 if payments is slipping too.

explanations.plan: Targeted: general sick-wave overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P2: overtime for 8 general agents 13:00-15:00, plus delayed general breaks and IVR callback, for ₹2,880. Predicted service level is 85.5% for 12:00-15:30 against an 80% target.
General is short because of a sick wave, not extra demand. There are 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4, and only 9 agents were on the phones at 08:00 against 15 planned. Calls (23 vs 23.5 forecast) and handle time (384s vs 375s) are close to plan. With no action, service level is predicted to fall to 75.5% over 12:00-15:30, with general at 72.7%. P2 adds cover directly on general and lifts both queues: general to 84.9% and payments to 86.0%. Abandons drop from 5.2% to 3.5%, and rest of day is predicted at 91.6%. It breaks no policies.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but only reaches 79.4%, just under target. Its general queue sits right at 80.0% with no margin, and abandons are 4.7%.
Trade-off: P3 costs the same ₹2,880 but does worse overall: 84.3%, abandons 3.7%, rest of day 90.8%. It moves cross-skilled agents off payments, which drops payments to 82.9%, while general gets slightly more (86.2% vs 84.9%).
Trade-off: P2 leaves payments staff in place. That matters because payments also has high absence today (6 against a usual 2.6).
Watch: Check that enough of the 8 general agents actually accept the overtime; if uptake is low, the 85.5% forecast won't hold. Keep watching payments absence. The diagnosis rests on only one interval of data, so re-check service level after the next interval or two.

explanations.plan: No-cost: breaks, cross-skill move and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: the no-cost plan (delay Payments breaks, move 2 cross-skilled agents from General, IVR callback) lifts the 14:15-16:15 service level to 88.6% against an 80% target.
A sick wave, mostly 'Unplanned leave - family function', has left Payments at 55 agents vs 62.4 expected and General at 45 vs 57.6. Call volume and handle times are near forecast. Even with no action, the window is predicted at 87.5% (Payments 84.7%), so the target is already met. P1 costs nothing and shores up Payments, the weaker queue, raising it to 87.6%. Abandons ease slightly from 2.5% to 2.4%. No policy issues and no escalation needed.
Trade-off: General gives up some headroom, falling from 91.1% to 89.8% while 2 agents help Payments. It stays well above 80%.
Trade-off: Rest-of-day service level dips slightly to 90.8% (vs 91.2% with no action).
Trade-off: P3 does best (89.4% overall, Payments 89.6%, abandons 1.9%, rest of day 92.1%) but costs INR 945 and uses the last of the overtime budget, leaving nothing for later surprises.
Trade-off: P2 gets Payments to 88.0% and abandons to 2.1% for INR 537, but it cancels coaching. P4 (INR 312) barely improves on doing nothing.
Trade-off: Doing nothing also meets target, but Payments would sit lower at 84.7%.
Watch: Watch Payments service level and General as the 2 agents leave (14:15-15:30), and look for any further absences. If either queue trends toward 80%, consider P3's overtime, which would use the last of the overtime budget.

explanations.plan: No-cost: break shift, small cross-skill move, payments callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: no-cost break shift, general callback and one evening cross-skill move lifts service level to 83.7% for 15:00-20:00, with payments back above the 80% target.
The problem is fewer agents, not more calls: payments has 13 absences against a usual 2.6 and general has 15 against 2.4, mostly 'Unplanned leave - family function'. Volume and handle time are close to plan. Doing nothing gives 81.3% overall, but payments drops to 77.8%, below the 80% target. P1 delays 15:00-16:00 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes, runs IVR callback on general 15:00-16:00, and moves 1 cross-skilled agent from general to payments 19:00-20:00. That brings payments to 82.0% and keeps general at 86.2%, with abandons falling from 4.6% to 3.9%. It costs nothing and breaks no policy. It is the cheapest plan that hits target on both queues.
Trade-off: Payments has the least headroom: 82.0% against the 80% target. P2 gives 86.5% on payments and 86.9% overall for INR 906, but it cancels coaching and pushes 20% of payments status/refund contacts to chat.
Trade-off: P3 (INR 1,098) and P4 (INR 1,350) add only small further gains: 87.2% and 87.7% overall, with abandons at 3.5% and 3.3%. They rely on chat deflection, a 2-agent move or overtime.
Trade-off: Risk to general is minimal. It goes from 86.3% to 86.2% under P1 despite giving up 1 agent 19:00-20:00. General callers in 15:00-16:00 will be offered callbacks instead of waiting.
Trade-off: Delayed breaks put more strain on agents who are already covering for absent colleagues.
Watch: Watch payments service level, especially into the evening. Its margin is only 2 points above target. If it slips toward 80%, or more absences come in, move up to P2 (INR 906). No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Strong recovery: overtime + breaks + callback + chat
explanations.text:
Approve P4 (overtime + delayed breaks + callback + chat deflection): the only option predicted to reach the 80% target, at 81.5% for 13:45-15:45, extra cost INR 3,336.
General is short on agents because of a sick wave. It has 26.1 agents on the phones against 32 planned, and 6 agents went home unwell after lunch. Call volume and handle time are normal, so this is a capacity problem. With no action, service level is predicted at 62.9% for 13:45-15:45, with 9.0% abandons. P4 combines offering overtime to 22 agents (12 General, 10 Payments) for 14:15-15:15, delaying breaks by 45 min, IVR callback, and 20% chat deflection on simple enquiries. It is the only plan predicted to clear 80%: 81.5% overall, abandons down to 3.4%, and rest of day 91.3% versus 83.5% with no action. It breaks no policy and needs no escalation.
Trade-off: Cost: P4 adds INR 3,336. The cheaper options fall short of target: P3 costs INR 816 and reaches 73.5%, P2 costs INR 2,520 and reaches 72.8%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: abandons fall from 9.0% to 3.4%. P3 gets to 5.7%. P1 costs nothing but does slightly worse than no action (60.8%), so it is not worth doing alone.
Trade-off: Other queue: Payments stays the weaker queue under P4 at 78.5%, just under target on its own, while General reaches 85.5%. The 80% target is met on the combined figure only.
Trade-off: Risk: P4 depends on enough agents accepting overtime. If uptake is low, the result will drift toward P3's 73.5%.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 14:15 and Payments service level each interval. If uptake is short or Payments stays below about 78%, consider widening chat deflection or the callback window. Also watch for further sick-home logs after 13:42.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1, the no-cost rebalance: it lifts the 14:30-16:30 service level to 89.5% against the 80% target at no extra cost.
A sick wave is behind the 12% staffing shortfall. Payments has 11 absences against a usual 2.8, and general has 10 against a usual 2.6. Call volume and handle time are roughly on plan. P1 delays payments breaks from 14:30-15:00 by 45 minutes, moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments between 14:30 and 15:30, and offers IVR callback on payments from 15:00 to 15:30. That raises payments from 83.4% to 87.6% and general from 91.4% to 92.1%, for 89.5% overall. Abandons fall from 2.2% to 1.5% and the rest-of-day figure rises to 94.7%. It costs INR 0, follows policy, and is the cheapest plan that clearly beats the target.
Trade-off: Doing nothing (P0) already predicts 86.8%, above target, but payments sits at only 83.4%, which leaves little buffer if more agents go home. P1 adds margin for free.
Trade-off: P4 (demand-side relief) costs INR 264 and gives 95.2%, with 94.2% on payments and 0.5% abandons. That is noticeably better customer impact for a small cost and is worth considering if you want more headroom.
Trade-off: P2 (INR 720, 92.7%) and P3 (INR 1,344, 94.7%, 0.4% abandons) cost more and do not beat P4 on service level.
Trade-off: Moving 3 agents out of general carries a small risk to that queue, but general is still predicted at 92.1%, higher than under no action.
Watch: Watch payments service level closely from 14:30 to 15:30. If it drops toward 80% or more absences come in, step up to P4's chat deflection or P2's overtime. Also confirm general holds above target while the 3 agents are moved. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: No-cost: IVR callback in the evening dip
explanations.text:
Approve P1: switch on IVR callback for the evening dip (general 18:00-20:00, payments 18:30-20:00) at no extra cost.
Both queues are short because of a sick wave. Payments has 15 absences against a usual 2.8, and general has 13 against 2.6, mostly agents who went home unwell after lunch. Call volume is close to forecast, so this is a staffing gap, not a demand spike. Service level has dropped to 49% on payments and 61.6% on general. Even so, the forecast for the disruption window (15:30-19:45) is that service level recovers above the 80% target without intervention: 89.2% with no action. P1 is the cheapest plan that meets target. It lifts the window to 89.6% (89.6% on both queues) and trims abandons from 2.6% to 2.4%, costs ₹0 and has no policy issues. Rest of day stays at 87.9%.
Trade-off: P1's gain over doing nothing is small (+0.4 points, 0.2 points fewer abandons). Its main value is giving customers a callback option during the evening at no cost.
Trade-off: P3 (chat deflection, callback and light overtime) reaches 94.4% in the window, 93.6% for the rest of day and 1.5% abandons, for ₹1,632. That is more headroom if absences keep rising.
Trade-off: P4 gives the strongest result (94.9% window, 1.3% abandons) at ₹3,252. P2's overtime-only plan costs ₹2,520 but is weaker than P3.
Trade-off: Both queues stay balanced under P1 (89.6% each), so neither queue is protected at the other's expense.
Watch: Payments is the queue to watch: it is furthest behind right now (49%) and has the higher absence count. If more agents go home, or payments service level is still not recovering by about 17:00, move to P3 for ₹1,632. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: No-cost: break shift, cross-skill loan and callback on general
explanations.text:
Approve P1: a no-cost mix of break shifts, a 2-agent cross-skill loan and IVR callback on General, predicted to lift service level to 82.3% (target 80%) for 12:45-14:45.
The problem is unplanned absence, not demand. Accounts & General has 6 absences against a usual 2.4 per day (2 called in sick, 4 sent home unwell). Agents on the phones dropped to 27 against 33 planned at 12:30, and service level fell to 58.2%. Call volume is roughly normal (+4.7% for the day). If we do nothing, the window is predicted at 79.2%, just under target, with General at 71.6%. P1 delays General breaks in 13:45-14:45 by 45 minutes, moves 2 cross-skilled agents from Payments to General (12:45-15:00) and turns on IVR callback for General. That takes the window to 82.3% and abandons from 5.0% to 4.3% at no extra cost. It is the cheapest plan that meets target and follows policy.
Trade-off: Cost vs. margin: P1 is free but clears the target by only 2.3 points, and General stays below target at 78.3%. P4 costs INR 630 for 84.5%, with General at 82.2% and 3.9% abandons.
Trade-off: Customer impact: P2 or P3 (INR 3,150 each) give the strongest result: 86.2% and 87.9% overall, General at 83.6% and 87.9%, abandons down to 2.8% and 3.0%.
Trade-off: Other queue: lending 2 agents does not hurt Payments, which is predicted at 85.4% vs 84.8% with no action.
Trade-off: Execution risk: P1 relies on callback uptake and break delays landing as planned; there is no overtime buffer if another agent goes home.
Watch: Watch General service level and agent headcount through 14:45. If General stays well below 78% or another absence occurs, move to P4 (INR 630) or P2 (INR 3,150) overtime.

explanations.plan: Demand smoothing for general
explanations.text:
Approve P4 (demand smoothing on general): predicted 80.9% service level for 14:30-16:30 at ₹372 extra, the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target.
This is a capacity problem, not a demand one. There were 9 unplanned absences on general against a usual 2.4: 4 called in sick and 5 were sent home unwell. Call volume is on forecast (564 vs 568). With no action, the window is predicted at 79.0%, with general at 74.5%. P4 delays breaks on both queues, adds IVR callback on general, and deflects 15% of balance and new-offer enquiries to chat. That brings general up to 80.4% and keeps payments at 81.3%. Predicted abandon rate falls to 3.5% from 4.2%, and rest-of-day service level rises to 88.6%. Diagnosis confidence is medium because the detector's staffing figures don't match the floor counts after 13:45.
Trade-off: P1 (₹0) and P2 (₹300) cost less but both miss the target, at 78.1% and 77.4%. Both also move cross-skilled agents off payments, cutting payments to 78.7% and 79.9%.
Trade-off: P3 (overtime) reaches 81.7% with general at 79.6%. It costs ₹1,740, nearly five times P4, and depends on agents accepting overtime offers.
Trade-off: P4 leaves payments staff in place, so the other queue is protected. The customer impact is that some general callers are pushed to callback or chat instead of a live agent.
Trade-off: P4 clears the target by only 0.9 points, so there is little margin if absences grow.
Watch: Watch general-queue service level and chat uptake from 15:00. If more agents are sent home, or deflection falls short and general drops below about 78%, move to P3's overtime offers.

explanations.plan: Larger overtime offer for the last half-hour
explanations.text:
Approve R1: move 2 cross-skilled agents to general, offer overtime to 12 general agents 19:30-20:00, plus chat deflection and IVR callback. Predicted 81.9% service level for 19:00-20:00 at ₹792.
General is short of agents because of a sick wave: 9 absences against a usual 2.4. Call volume is normal (564 vs 568 forecast), so the fix is adding capacity, not managing demand. Doing nothing leaves the window at 68.6%, with general at 44.4%. The no-cost and low-cost options only reach 68.0–73.3%. R1 is the cheapest plan that clears the 80% target. It lifts general to 74.0%, keeps payments at 88.3% and cuts abandons from 10.5% to 5.0%. Diagnosis confidence is medium: recent on-phone counts from 13:45 don't match the detector's staffing figures.
Trade-off: Cost: ₹792, against ₹252 for P3, which reaches only 73.3% and leaves general at 56.1%.
Trade-off: R2 (20 overtime offers, ₹1,332) gives a bigger margin: 87.5% overall, general 81.1%, abandons 3.9%. That costs ₹540 more than R1.
Trade-off: Overall service level clears the target, but general alone stays below 80% at 74.0%. Its customers still wait longer than payments customers.
Trade-off: Risk to payments is low: it holds at 88.3%. Moving a 3rd agent (P4) would drop payments to 84.4% and make things worse overall (68.0%).
Trade-off: R1 depends on overtime take-up. If fewer than 12 accept, the window will likely fall short of 80%.
Watch: Track overtime acceptances before 19:30. If take-up is well short of 12, consider widening the offer toward R2. Also watch general queue service level and any further sent-home-unwell entries after the last one at 14:20. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: P4 refocused: more overtime in the 13:00 hour, chat deflection on both queues
explanations.text:
Approve R1: heavy payments overtime plus chat deflection on both queues lifts service level to 73.2% for 12:30-14:30, still short of the 80% target, at ₹14,148.
The drop is caused by system slowness, not extra calls. P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 is freezing core banking screens, and payments handle time has risen to 561 s against a forecast of about 295 s. Volume, call mix and absences are all normal. Doing nothing leaves 12:30-14:30 at 32.8% (payments 19.1%), with 20.2% of calls abandoned. No plan reaches 80% in this window, so R1 was chosen as the best available. It predicts 73.2% overall (payments 70.2%, general 77.1%), cuts abandons to 6.8%, and lifts the rest of the day to 89.6%. It offers overtime to 55 payments agents for 13:00-14:00 and 25 for 14:00-15:00. It also deflects 20% of selected enquiry types to chat on both queues, delays payments breaks by 45 min, and offers IVR callbacks on payments.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same (₹14,148) and gives the same 73.2% overall with no break delays. It favours payments (73.7%) but leaves general lower (72.7% vs 77.1%) and abandons slightly higher (7.2% vs 6.8%).
Trade-off: P4 is ₹816 cheaper (₹13,332) but reaches only 66.0% with 8.5% abandons. P3 (₹8,640) reaches 55.1%. The no-cost options P0 and P1 stay around 32%.
Trade-off: R1 depends on about 55 agents accepting overtime in the 13:00 hour. If fewer accept, payments service will fall back towards the P4/P3 levels.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 13:00 and payments handle time against the incident. If INC-20261102-2029 is resolved early, scale back the 14:00-15:00 overtime. If it worsens or overtime uptake is low, expect payments to stay well below 70%.

explanations.plan: Maximum compliant recovery with chat and callback extended
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (overtime for 16 general agents, break shifts, callbacks and late chat deflection) for ₹3,852, but involve the duty manager: it lifts 13:15-15:15 service level only to 59.9%, well short of the 80% target.
Payments calls are taking much longer, not arriving in greater numbers. Handle time rose from about 306 s to 561 s against a 295 s forecast, in line with P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 (core banking screens freezing, account-summary API over 8 s). Service level has dropped to 2.2%, with 69 abandons in the 12:15 interval. No compliant plan reaches 80%. R2 is the best one that follows policy. It predicts 59.9% on both queues (payments 59.9%, general 59.9%) and cuts abandons to 10.0%, compared with 46.6% and 15.4% if we do nothing. Rest of day recovers to 85.3%.
Trade-off: Against R1 (₹3,600, 57.3%): R2 adds ₹252 and 2.6 points, and payments improves from 57.0% to 59.9%.
Trade-off: Against P1 (free, 48.1%, 13.2% abandon): R2 costs ₹3,852 but gives nearly 12 points more and fewer abandoned customers.
Trade-off: P4 (64.4%) and P2 (55.8%) score higher or similar but breach CX-01. The outage message targets upi_payment_failed, which is not a rising reason, so they are excluded.
Trade-off: R2 balances the two queues evenly. P3 (57.0%) leaves general lower at 52.4%.
Trade-off: Delayed breaks and overtime add agent fatigue during an already stressful incident.
Watch: Escalate now. Even the best compliant plan is predicted at about 60%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should decide on further levers and push for incident resolution. Track payments handle time against 561 s and incident INC-20261102-2029 status, overtime uptake (16 agents needed), and payments service level once breaks shift at 14:15.

explanations.plan: Staffing-only, overtime split across queues
explanations.text:
Approve P4 (split overtime, delayed breaks, coaching cancelled) for 14:00-16:00, but it only lifts service level to 40.6% against an 80% target, so bring in the duty manager now.
The drop is caused by slow systems, not extra calls. Payments handle time rose to 561 s against a forecast of about 295 s. This matches P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 (core banking screens freezing, account-summary API over 8 s p95). Volume and absences are normal. No plan reaches 80%. P4 gives the best predicted service level for 14:00-16:00 at 40.6%, compared with 38.7% for doing nothing. It also cuts abandons from 20.7% to 19.3% and costs INR 1,560. It is the only plan that clearly helps both queues: payments goes to 44.4% and general to 35.4%. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 75.4%.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing, but at 38.8% it is barely better than doing nothing.
Trade-off: P3 and R1 cost more (INR 2,088) and give slightly lower abandons (18.6%) and payments service level (45.1%). However, their overall service level is lower (40.2%), and general falls to 33.5%.
Trade-off: Putting all 4 overtime agents on payments (P3) helps payments at the expense of general. P4 splits the overtime, which protects general.
Trade-off: P4 does not use callback or chat deflection. Those levers add cost but gave little extra benefit in the predictions.
Watch: Escalation is required. The best compliant plan is predicted at about 41% for 14:00-16:00, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should be involved, because the only real fix is resolving the system incident. Track progress on INC-20261102-2029 and payments handle time. Also watch general queue service level and abandons after overtime starts at 14:30.

explanations.plan: P4 refined: overtime + chat on both queues, no break delays
explanations.text:
Approve R1: overtime on both queues plus chat deflection, no break delays. Predicted 79.1% service level for 11:30-13:30, just short of the 80% target, at ₹16,800.
Payments calls are taking much longer than planned (handle time up to 479 s against a 313 s forecast), most likely because of a slow internal tool. IT has not confirmed this, so please check with them. Call volume and staffing look normal, so the fix is extra capacity and fewer calls. No plan reaches 80% in the disruption window, and R1 comes closest at 79.1%. It offers overtime to 35 payments agents (12:00-14:00) and 10 more (14:00-15:00), plus 5 general agents (12:00-14:00). It also moves 20% of simple enquiries on both queues to chat. Breaks stay as scheduled. Payments is predicted at 70.8% and general at 90.6%, with abandons at 6.4% against 18.0% if we do nothing. Rest of day is predicted at 90.9%.
Trade-off: R1 costs ₹816 more than P4 (₹15,984), which reaches 77.4%. P4 is better for payments (74.0% vs 70.8%) and abandons slightly less (5.9% vs 6.4%), but it delays breaks and general falls to 81.9%.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same ₹16,800 but is worse on every measure: 77.3% overall, payments 69.5%.
Trade-off: P3 saves about ₹3,500 (₹13,320) but only reaches 70.8%, with 8.1% abandons.
Trade-off: The no-cost and low-cost options (P1 and P2, ₹0 to ₹1,224) leave the window at 40-46% with around 15-18% abandons. P1 even pushes payments down to 21.4%.
Watch: Payments remains the weak queue at 70.8% under R1. Watch overtime uptake: if fewer than about 35 payments agents accept, service will fall short. Follow up with IT on the suspected slow tool. If it is fixed, handle times should drop and some of the overtime could be released.

explanations.plan: Targeted overtime plus general break delays and a longer payments chat window
explanations.text:
Approve R2: overtime for 13 payments agents, callbacks on both queues, a 45-minute delay to general breaks and chat deflection. It is predicted to reach 81.2% service level for 12:15-14:15 at an extra cost of ₹2,004.
Payments handle time has climbed from about 291-299 s forecast to 560 s by 12:00. Call volume and staffing are on plan, so the problem is longer calls, not more of them. The likely cause is the CardMax slowness ticket INC-20261019-1835. That link is not yet confirmed: the ticket is a P4 opened at 12:05. Service level recovered to 96.7% at 12:00 only because 50 agents were on the phones against 39 planned. With no action, service level is predicted to fall to 68.0% (payments 63.4%) during 12:15-14:15. R2 is the only option that reaches the 80% target over that window: 81.2% overall, payments 78.5%, general 84.7%, abandon rate 5.5%. It breaks no policy rules. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 89.7%.
Trade-off: Cost: R2 costs ₹2,004. That is ₹204 more than R1 (₹1,800), which only reaches 74.8%. It is ₹156 less than P2 and P3 (₹2,160 each), which reach only 77.4% and 74.5%.
Trade-off: Payments stays below target: even under R2, payments is predicted at 78.5% while general carries the overall figure at 84.7%.
Trade-off: Effect on general: R2 delays general breaks 13:15-13:45 by 45 minutes. General still does well in this window (84.7%, against 73.8% with no action).
Trade-off: Rest of day: P2 has a slightly better rest-of-day figure (90.0% against 89.7%) and is close on abandon rate, but it misses the target during the disruption window.
Trade-off: The no-cost option, P1, barely helps: 69.0% overall and 62.3% on payments.
Watch: Watch payments handle time and the CardMax ticket. If handle time keeps rising beyond 560 s, or the ticket is confirmed and not fixed by 14:15, these predictions will be optimistic and the plan should be reviewed. Escalation is not flagged. Check overtime uptake from the 13 agents by 12:45, because the plan depends on it.

explanations.plan: Targeted, with a wider break shift and the 15:00 hour protected
explanations.text:
Approve R2: targeted IVR messaging and callbacks with a wider break shift. It is the best available plan at 72.6% over 13:00-15:00 but still short of the 80% target.
Payments handle time has nearly doubled (560 s against 299 s forecast at 12:00), while calls and staffing are on plan. The likely cause is slowness in the CardMax card tool after this morning's release (ticket INC-20261019-1835, P4, link not confirmed). Doing nothing is predicted to give 57.2% (payments 49.2%) with 12.7% abandons. R2 raises the window to 72.6% (payments 66.0%, general 80.2%) and cuts abandons to 6.5%. It also gives the best rest-of-day figure at 86.4%, for INR 1,143 with no policy violations. No plan reaches 80% for the window, so R2 was chosen as the strongest option.
Trade-off: R1 costs only INR 168 and gives 70.1% (payments 64.0%, abandons 6.9%). R2 adds 2.5 points and protects the 15:00 hour for INR 975 more, mainly by cancelling payments coaching 15:30-16:15.
Trade-off: P3 costs the same INR 1,143 as R2 but delivers only 65.2%, so R2 is clearly better value at that spend.
Trade-off: Moving breaks shifts load later: general breaks are delayed too, but general stays healthy at 80.2%, so the other queue is not put at risk.
Trade-off: Payments customers still face 66.0% service level during the window. Callers with declined cards will hear a known-issue message and some will be offered callback or chat.
Watch: Watch payments handle time and the CardMax ticket. If handle time keeps rising beyond 560 s, or the ticket is confirmed and not fixed by 15:00, the gap will last longer than planned and payments service will fall further. In that case, consider pushing to raise the ticket's priority and involving the duty manager.

explanations.plan: Bigger overtime on general and payments over the midday peak
explanations.text:
Approve R1: overtime for 48 general and 10 payments agents (11:15-13:00). It is the best available plan, but it still misses the 80% target (70.9% predicted for 10:45-12:45).
General handle time jumped to 744.9 s at 10:30 against 363.0 s forecast. Volume and attendance are normal, which points to a slow tool or process. With no action, service level for 10:45-12:45 is predicted at 45.1%, general queue only 16.0%, and abandons 18.5%. No plan reaches 80%. R1 gets closest at 70.9%, with general at 41.8%, payments at 93.8% and abandons at 7.1%, for INR 13,155. It also lifts rest of day to 84.0%. Its other actions are delaying general breaks 10:45-11:45 by 45 min, cancelling general coaching 11:00-11:59, and 20% chat deflection on balance, new-offer and refund-status calls. Before committing, confirm the slowness with the floor and IT. There is no incident ticket yet, and the spike shows in only one interval.
Trade-off: Cost: R1 costs INR 13,155. The next best, P4, costs INR 7,485 but reaches only 57.7% (general 31.3%), with 11.3% abandons versus 7.1%.
Trade-off: R2 costs about the same (INR 13,245) but predicts only 57.7% in the disruption window. Its rest-of-day figure is slightly higher (84.7% vs 84.0%), so it does less for the current problem.
Trade-off: The cheap plans P1 (INR 75) and P2 (INR 555) do not help. They predict 43.5% and 44.8%, no better than doing nothing (45.1%), and general falls to around 10%.
Trade-off: Other queue: R1 adds 10 payments overtime agents, so payments is protected and rises to 93.8% rather than being drained to cover general.
Trade-off: Customer impact: R1 has no IVR callbacks. Chat deflection is the only demand lever, so customer friction stays modest.
Trade-off: The general queue stays weak at 41.8% even under R1.
Watch: Watch general handle time each interval and check with IT whether a system issue is confirmed. If handle time returns towards about 363 s, scale back the overtime. If it stays high and general remains far below 80%, consider involving the duty manager. Also track overtime uptake, since the prediction assumes 48 general and 10 payments agents accept.

explanations.plan: Lower cost: whole-window break delays, callbacks and chat, no overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (whole-window break delays, callbacks and chat on both queues, no overtime) for Rs 1,164, and bring in the duty manager: it is the best plan within policy but reaches only 67.6% against the 80% target for 13:00-15:00.
General's handle time has roughly doubled since 10:30 (about 345 s to 644-745 s, against a forecast of about 370 s). Call volume is below forecast and sickness is normal, so the likely cause is ticket INC-20261104-2401: knowledge-base search is timing out. The link is likely but not confirmed, because the ticket was opened an hour after handle time rose. With no action, the window is predicted at 45.2% with 14.8% abandons. R2 lifts this to 67.6% with 6.7% abandons and 85.6% for the rest of the day. No plan within policy reaches 80%. Escalation is required because R2 is below the 70% line (ESC-02). The duty manager should decide whether to accept this and should push for a fix to the knowledge-base incident.
Trade-off: R1 is the only option above 70% (72.9%, General 56.4%, 5.7% abandons) for Rs 2,244, but it breaks overtime rule OT-04. Expected overtime would be Rs 15,264 against today's Rs 15,000 budget, so only the duty manager could approve it.
Trade-off: P3 costs more (Rs 1,524) yet predicts only 61.0%, because its break delays cover just 13:00-14:00. R2 does better for less money.
Trade-off: Even under R2, General stays weak at 45.3% while Payments reaches 85.3%. General's callers carry most of the impact.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but barely helps (46.3%). P2 costs Rs 264 and reaches 53.1%, which leaves General at 36.6%.
Trade-off: Delaying breaks across the whole window will strain agents, and break-time cover after 15:00 will need watching.
Watch: Watch General's handle time and the progress of INC-20261104-2401. If knowledge-base search recovers, service should improve quickly; if handle time stays near 700 s, ask the duty manager about R1's overtime. Also check that chat deflection and callback uptake are actually reducing General's queue.

explanations.plan: Full outage response with maximum overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R1 (full UPI outage response with 55 overtime agents) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best compliant plan but still only reaches 67% against the 80% target.
This is a UPI outage, not a staffing problem. Payments calls hit 201 at 13:30 against a forecast of about 96–99, driven by 'UPI payment failed' calls tied to P1 incident INC-20261027-4076. Service level fell to 2.5%. R1 combines four actions: an IVR outage message for UPI failures, overtime for 55 payments agents from 14:15 to 16:00, 20% chat deflection of payment-status and refund-status calls, and delayed breaks on both queues. It lifts the 13:45–15:45 window from 32.1% (no action) to 67.0%, with payments at 59.0% and general at 84.3%. Abandons drop from 26.0% to 7.5%, and rest of day reaches 83.3%. Extra cost is ₹12,657. Escalation: 67% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved. Even maximum compliant effort will not hit target while the outage continues.
Trade-off: Cost: R1 costs ₹12,657, about ₹3,000 more than P3 (₹9,675, 53.6%) and P4 (₹10,935, 54.6%), but gains roughly 13 points and cuts abandons to 7.5%.
Trade-off: R2 costs more (₹13,917) and does worse at 63.8%, because it skips the IVR outage message.
Trade-off: The cheap options do not help: P1 (₹225) and P2 (₹0) leave service level around 29–31%, slightly worse than doing nothing.
Trade-off: Risk to the general queue is low. Delaying general breaks still leaves general at 84.3%, up from 69.3% with no action.
Trade-off: Customer impact: some payments callers will hear an outage message or be pushed to chat rather than reaching an agent.
Watch: Track overtime uptake: R1 assumes 55 agents accept from 14:15. Watch payments service level against the 59% prediction and the progress of incident INC-20261027-4076. If the UPI fix lands early, consider releasing overtime. If uptake is short or call volume keeps climbing, the duty manager should consider further steps.

explanations.plan: No-cost staffing and callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: delay payments breaks, move 4 cross-skilled agents to payments and turn on IVR callback, at no extra cost, for a predicted 87.3% service level against the 80% target.
Payments demand spiked because of the UPI outage (P1 incident INC-20261027-4076). 'UPI payment failed' calls are at 154 against 68.8 expected, and service level fell to 2.5% at 13:30. This is not a staffing problem. For the disruption window (14:30-16:30), even doing nothing is predicted to reach 86.6% (payments 83.0%). P1 lifts that to 87.3% (payments 84.1%) and cuts abandons from 3.0% to 2.6% at zero cost. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that meets the target. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 90.6%.
Trade-off: Cost: P1 costs nothing. P4 (cancel coaching, move 6 agents) reaches the best result, 87.8% with 2.5% abandons, but costs INR 450 and loses general coaching. P3 costs INR 588, uses the last overtime budget and does slightly worse (87.1%).
Trade-off: Customer impact: P1 improves payments abandons from 3.0% to 2.6% compared with no action. P2 costs INR 228 and predicts 86.3%, which is worse than doing nothing.
Trade-off: Other queue: moving 4 agents drops general only slightly, from 94.5% to 94.3%, still well above target.
Trade-off: Staff: payments agents' breaks are pushed back 45 minutes between 15:00 and 16:00.
Watch: Watch payments volume against the UPI incident status. If the outage lasts beyond 16:00 or calls keep rising past the 201 seen at 13:30, consider P4 next. Overtime (P3) would use the last of the budget, so treat it as a last resort. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Full response with remaining overtime budget
explanations.text:
Approve P3: full response with the remaining overtime budget. It is the only option that reaches the 80% target (81.4%) for 15:15-17:15, at ₹1,902 extra.
The surge is caused by the UPI outage (P1 incident INC-20261027-4076), not by staffing. 'UPI payment failed' calls are running at 2.24x normal, and absences and handle time are normal. So the fix needs both lower outage demand and more payments capacity. P3 combines an IVR outage message, 20% chat deflection, overtime for 7 payments agents (15:45-16:45), cancelled payments coaching, 8 cross-skilled agents moved from general (16:00-17:00), delayed breaks and IVR callback. It is predicted to lift service level to 81.4% overall (payments 77.8%, general 90.0%) and cut abandons to 3.2%, versus 57.0% and 10.5% with no action. Rest-of-day service level improves to 86.6%. There are no policy violations and no escalation is needed.
Trade-off: P2 (outage message, deflection, agent move, delayed breaks) costs ₹792, ₹1,110 less than P3, but reaches only 75.8% (payments 69.8%) with 5.0% abandons. It falls short of target.
Trade-off: P1 (no-cost shuffle, ₹450) does no better than doing nothing: 56.8% vs 57.0%, with payments at 44.9%. Moving agents alone doesn't touch the outage demand.
Trade-off: Risk to general is low. General holds at 90.0% under P3 despite losing 8 agents for 16:00-17:00.
Trade-off: P3 uses the remaining overtime budget, leaving no overtime headroom if the outage runs past 17:15.
Watch: Payments service level and abandons from 15:45, when overtime starts, and again at 16:00, when the agent move and callback begin. Also watch the status of INC-20261027-4076. If UPI isn't restored by about 17:00, or payments stays well below 77.8%, involve the duty manager, because there is no overtime budget left.

explanations.plan: Outage message, overtime and chat deflection, lighter break shift
explanations.text:
Approve R2: outage message, overtime on both queues and chat deflection. It is predicted to lift service level to 82.5% over 12:15-14:15 for ₹9,084.
The spike is driven by card_declined calls from P1 incident INC-20261016-7996, the card gateway outage. Card_declined calls are running at 2.26x normal, and service level has fallen to 44.6%. If we do nothing, the window is predicted at 47.4%, with payments at 34.6% and a 14.8% abandon rate. R2 tackles the outage directly with a known-issue IVR message for card_declined callers. It adds overtime for 35 payments and 10 general agents, deflects 20% of selected status and enquiry calls to chat on both queues, and uses a shorter 30-minute break shift. Predicted results are 82.5% overall (payments 79.6%, general 87.9%), abandons down to 4.4%, and 91.8% for the rest of the day. It is the cheapest option that reaches the 80% target and breaks no policy.
Trade-off: R1 also reaches target (80.5%) but costs more (₹9,720) and does slightly worse on service level (82.5%) and abandons (4.4% vs 5.3%).
Trade-off: P3 (₹3,600, 72.6%) and P4 (₹4,050, 73.9%) are much cheaper but miss the 80% target, leaving payments at about 70-72%.
Trade-off: The no-cost plans miss the target by a wide margin: P2 reaches 55.6% and P1 45.6%. P1 actually makes things worse by pulling agents from general.
Trade-off: R2 protects the general queue (87.9%) rather than borrowing from it. Payments is still just under 80% on its own at 79.6%.
Trade-off: It depends on enough agents accepting overtime and on customers taking up chat deflection.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance and card_declined volume each interval. If the gateway incident runs past 14:00, extend the IVR outage message. If the incident is resolved early, cut overtime back to save cost.

explanations.plan: No-cost: shift breaks, callback and keep the outage message running
explanations.text:
Approve P1: shift breaks, add callback and keep the outage message running. Predicted 86.7% service level for 13:00–15:00 at no extra cost.
The extra payments calls are most likely caused by the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 incident INC-20261016-7996, opened 11:45). Card_declined calls ran at 4.95x normal and account for about 228 of the roughly 287 excess calls. Service level fell as low as 10.1% at 12:15. P1 is predicted to reach 86.7% over 13:00–15:00, against the 80% target, with payments at 88.1% and general at 84.3%. Abandons are predicted at 3.2%. It costs nothing extra and breaks no policy rules. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 91.8%.
Trade-off: Doing nothing (P0) is also predicted to meet target, at 84.0% with 3.8% abandons. That leaves less margin, with general at 81.7%. P1 adds headroom at the same zero cost.
Trade-off: P2 gives a higher 91.7% (2.6% abandons, rest of day 95.0%) for ₹552, using chat deflection. It is worth considering if you want a bigger buffer.
Trade-off: P3 is strongest at 95.5% with 1.3% abandons, but costs ₹3,672 in overtime for 30 agents. P4 reaches 89.4% for ₹1,440.
Trade-off: P1's rest-of-day figure (91.8%) is slightly below P0's (92.3%), likely because breaks move later and callbacks are handled afterwards.
Trade-off: Under P1, general is the weaker queue at 84.3%, because general breaks are also delayed. It stays above target.
Watch: Track the incident status and card_declined volume. If the outage runs beyond 15:00 or general service level drops toward 80%, step up to P2 (₹552). Also confirm the delayed breaks and the callback backlog are cleared after 15:00.

explanations.plan: Maximum recovery: all demand levers plus heavy overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P4: the only plan that reaches the 80% target, at 83.1% service level from 12:00-14:45 for ₹14,268 extra.
Payments calls hit 212 against 100 forecast at 11:45 and service level fell to 4.7%. The extra calls are mostly payment status and refund status enquiries, which matches incident INC-20261112-1271 (IMPS/NEFT transfers stuck pending after debit). With no action, the window is predicted at 33.1% with 24.6% abandons. P4 combines an IVR outage message, 20% chat deflection, callback, delayed breaks on both queues and overtime for payments agents (40 agents 12:30-13:30, then 25 agents 13:30-14:30). It is predicted to deliver 86.1% on payments and 77.8% on general, with abandons down to 4.2% and 90.8% for the rest of the day. It has no policy violations.
Trade-off: P3 costs ₹8,640, saving ₹5,628, but reaches only 67.4% (payments 64.6%) with 8.5% abandons, short of target.
Trade-off: P2 costs ₹1,668 and gives 50.5% with 12.9% abandons. That is much cheaper, but leaves payments customers at 44.2%.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but performs worse than doing nothing (29.6%). Its general-queue break delays drop general to 53.8%.
Trade-off: P4 also delays general breaks. General stays at 77.8%, slightly below 80%, and above general's 62.2% with no action.
Watch: P4 depends on overtime uptake (65 agent-slots in total). If fewer agents accept, expect results closer to P3. Also track the incident status: if INC-20261112-1271 runs past 14:00, the IVR message and chat deflection end before the window closes at 14:45 and will need extending. Check that general-queue service level holds near 78% while its breaks are delayed.

explanations.plan: Peak-only overtime plus both-queue breaks
explanations.text:
Approve P4: overtime for 25 payments agents 13:15-14:15, delay all breaks 12:45-13:45 by 45 min, and an IVR outage message, for ₹4,320 and a predicted 84.8% service level against the 80% target.
Payments calls are running about 97% over forecast because of incident INC-20261112-1271, where IMPS/NEFT transfers are stuck in 'pending' after the account has been debited. Service level recovered to 95.8% at 12:30 only because 51 agents were on phones against 36 planned. Doing nothing is predicted to give 68.2% for 12:45-14:45, with 7.3% of callers abandoning. P4 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It is predicted to give 84.8% over the window (payments 89.7%, general 76.5%), cut abandons to 3.6%, and lift the rest of the day to 93.0%.
Trade-off: P3 also reaches the target at 81.3% but costs more, ₹5,118. It also leans on chat deflection and callbacks, so P4 is both cheaper and better here.
Trade-off: P1 (no cost, 70.4%) and P2 (₹348, 74.5%) save money but both miss the 80% target, leaving abandons at 6.8% and 5.8%.
Trade-off: General is predicted at 76.5% under P4, slightly below P3's 76.9% and P2's 77.8%. This is because general breaks are also delayed and the overtime goes only to payments, so the general queue carries some risk below target.
Trade-off: P4 has no chat deflection or callback, so it depends on the 25 overtime agents actually accepting.
Watch: Check overtime uptake before 13:15; if well short of 25, consider P3's extra measures. Watch general queue service level and the incident status, as volume stays high until INC-20261112-1271 is fixed and the 14:15-14:45 period has no overtime cover.

explanations.plan: No-cost: push breaks to 15:00 and offer callbacks
explanations.text:
Approve P1: delay 14:00-15:00 breaks by 45 min and offer IVR callbacks on both queues, at no extra cost, lifting service level to 89.9% for 13:45-15:45.
The IMPS/NEFT payment hub fault (INC-20261112-1271) is resolved and payments calls are almost back to forecast (91 vs 85.8 at 13:30). Service level has been 100% since 13:00. Doing nothing would still give 85.7% overall, but general would sit at 79.9%, just under the 80% target. P1 costs nothing and brings general to 84.3% and payments to 94.1%. Abandons fall from 3.3% to 2.3%, and rest of day rises to 94.9%.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) also costs ₹0 but leaves general at 79.9%, below target, with 3.3% abandons.
Trade-off: P2 costs ₹324 for chat deflection, and it does slightly worse than P1 overall (89.6% vs 89.9%, general 83.5%, abandons 2.6%), so the spend isn't justified.
Trade-off: P3 gives the strongest result (93.6% overall, general 90.7%, abandons 1.7%, rest of day 96.4%) but costs ₹1,944 in overtime for a disruption that is already over.
Trade-off: P1 pushes agents' breaks back 45 minutes, and callbacks mean some customers get a call back rather than being answered straight away.
Watch: Watch the general queue, which has the least headroom at 84.3%, along with the callback queue and the delayed breaks through 14:00-15:00. If payments volume climbs again or general drops toward 80%, move up to P3's overtime.

explanations.plan: Overtime moved earlier into the worst hours
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (earlier overtime, chat deflection, break and coaching tweaks) for ₹15,579, and involve the duty manager: it lifts service level to about 59% for 11:15-15:30 but still falls short of the 80% target.
The surge is real customer demand from SMS campaign MKT-2026-825, sent at 10:15 to 700,000 people. Calls were 143 vs 85.3 forecast at 11:00 (+68%), driven mainly by loan enquiries at 2.02x normal. Service level has already dropped to 41.3%. Doing nothing predicts 32.8% (general queue 17.4%) and 19.4% abandons. R2 puts overtime into the worst hours: 34 general agents 11:45-13:45 and 30 more 13:45-14:45. It also deflects 20% of balance enquiries to chat, delays the 11:15-11:45 breaks by 45 minutes, lends 2 payments agents to general 15:00-16:00 and cancels general coaching 15:30-16:00. The prediction for 11:15-15:30 is 59.1% overall (payments 63.2%, general 55.4%), with 9.7% abandons and 72.3% for the rest of the day. It is the cheapest compliant plan among those that perform best. Escalation is flagged under ESC-02 because even this best compliant plan is predicted below the 70% line, so the duty manager should be involved.
Trade-off: R1 gives almost the same result (59.0%) but costs ₹16,029, which is ₹450 more than R2.
Trade-off: P3 predicts the highest service level (67.3%, 7.1% abandons) but depends on a known-issue IVR message. Policy CX-01 does not allow that message here because there is no confirmed outage, so it is not compliant.
Trade-off: P4 is compliant and cheaper at ₹13,680 but reaches only 53.4%, with the general queue at 44.1%.
Trade-off: The no-cost or low-cost options (P0 and P1 at ₹225, plus P2, which also breaks CX-01) stay around 32-34% and do not touch the problem.
Trade-off: Payments is not hurt by R2: it is predicted at 63.2% vs 50.4% with no action, because the 2 agents are only moved after 15:00.
Watch: Watch general-queue service level and abandons once overtime starts at 11:45, and check that enough of the 34 overtime offers are accepted. With the duty manager, decide whether to ask marketing to pause or reword the campaign, and how to handle the target shortfall.

explanations.plan: Policy-safe strongest: plan above plus overtime for 14:45-15:45
explanations.text:
Approve R2: the strongest policy-safe plan lifts disruption-window service level from 72.3% to 78.9%. That is still short of the 80% target, so it is the best available rather than a full fix.
The surge comes from SMS campaign MKT-2026-825, sent at 10:15 to 700,000 people. Loan enquiries are running at 2.02x normal, and service level has already fallen to 41.3%. No plan that follows policy reaches 80% for 12:00-15:30. R2 gets closest at 78.9%, with abandons down from 6.6% to 4.5% and rest of day at 87.7%. It combines callbacks on both queues, 20% chat deflection, delayed payments breaks, overtime for 6 general agents from 14:45 to 15:45, cancelled payments coaching, and a move of 5 cross-skilled agents to general from 15:00. Extra cost is INR 1,938.
Trade-off: Against R1: R2 costs INR 360 more (1,938 vs 1,578) for +1.5 points (78.9% vs 77.4%) and slightly fewer abandons (4.5% vs 4.8%).
Trade-off: P2 and P3 reach a similar level (77.9-78.1%) for little or no cost. Both break policy CX-01: they use a known-issue message, which needs a confirmed outage, and there is none here because the campaign is the cause. They are not usable.
Trade-off: General still lags at 74.1% while payments sits at 85.0%. Payments has headroom to give, so the move of 5 agents looks low-risk for that queue. However, payments also loses coaching and has breaks delayed by 45 minutes.
Trade-off: The no-cost option P1 gets only 73.7%, barely better than doing nothing (72.3%).
Watch: Watch general-queue service level and loan_enquiry volume after 12:00, and check whether the 6 overtime offers are accepted before 14:45. If general stays well below 74%, or the campaign drives a second wave, consider raising it with marketing or the duty manager.

explanations.plan: Policy-safe shift of breaks into spare hours
explanations.text:
Approve R1: shift breaks into quieter hours, cancel general coaching and deflect some status calls to chat. This lifts the 12:45-16:15 service level to 74.9%, short of the 80% target, for ₹225.
The spike in general calls comes from the 10:15 home-loan SMS (MKT-2026-825) sent to 700,000 people. Loan enquiries are running at 2.02x normal, and service level has already dropped to 41.3%. With no action, the disruption window is predicted at 71.6% (general 64.5%) with 5.8% abandons. R1 is the best plan that follows policy. It raises the window to 74.9% (general 68.2%, payments 83.7%), cuts abandons to 5.6% and lifts the rest of the day to 83.6%. No policy-compliant option reaches 80% in the window.
Trade-off: P2 (81.9%) and P3 (81.3%) are the only plans that hit 80%. Both rely on an IVR outage message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident; the campaign is planned demand, not a fault.
Trade-off: R2 costs ₹309 versus ₹225 and adds tail cover, but scores the same or slightly worse in the window (74.8%) and only adds 0.3 points to the rest of the day (83.9%).
Trade-off: P1 costs the same ₹225 but gets just 71.8%, raises abandons to 6.1% and drops payments to 79.6% by moving agents across. R1 keeps payments healthy at 83.7%.
Trade-off: R1 delays breaks on both queues, so agents will work longer stretches before resting.
Watch: General is still predicted at only 68.2%, so keep an eye on loan_enquiry volume and abandons through the afternoon. If the campaign keeps driving calls or service level stays well under 80%, bring in the duty manager to consider paid options or ask marketing about the SMS follow-up.

explanations.plan: Policy-compliant demand shaping plus evening break shift
explanations.text:
Approve R1: chat deflection, evening break shift, 5 agents moved and general coaching cancelled lifts service level to 82.2% for 15:30-19:30 at ₹615.
The general-queue surge comes from the 10:15 home-loan SMS (MKT-2026-825), with loan_enquiry calls running at 2.02x normal. Doing nothing leaves the window at 78.6%, just under the 80% target, with general at 69.4%. R1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and clears the target. It reaches 82.2% overall (general 74.2%, payments 93.5%), cuts abandons from 5.9% to 4.9%, and lifts the rest of the day to 83.0%.
Trade-off: Cheaper options miss the target. P4 costs ₹0 and reaches 79.1%, and P1 costs ₹75 and reaches 77.2%.
Trade-off: P2 (85.5%, ₹540) and P3 (86.6%, ₹921) score higher but break CX-01. They use a known-issue IVR message when there is no confirmed outage, because this is a campaign surge.
Trade-off: R2 costs ₹1,065 and predicts slightly lower overall service (82.0% vs 82.2%). Its abandon rate is only marginally better (4.8% vs 4.9%).
Trade-off: Payments gives up 5 cross-skilled agents from 16:00 to 18:00 but stays strong at a predicted 93.5%. General still sits below 80% on its own, at 74.2%.
Watch: Watch general-queue service level and loan_enquiry volume against forecast through 16:00-18:00. Check that chat deflection is actually taking about 20% of the targeted contacts. Confirm payments holds near 93% while its agents are moved.

explanations.plan: P4 plus payments support and more general overtime
explanations.text:
Approve R1: overtime and chat deflection on both queues, plus callback on General, lifts service level to 80.9% for 11:00–15:15 at ₹6,648.
General has been running 34–51% above forecast since 10:15. Service level fell to 24.6% at 10:45, with 22 abandoned calls. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so the cause is extra demand, and that demand is still unexplained. R1 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the disruption window (80.9% overall). It delays breaks on both queues by 30 minutes and offers overtime to 8 General agents (11:30–15:00) and 6 Payments agents (12:30–14:30). It also turns on 20% chat deflection for balance and payment-status enquiries and IVR callback on General. Predicted abandon rate drops from 6.9% to 3.7%, and rest-of-day service level rises to 85.6%.
Trade-off: Cost: R1 costs ₹6,648, about double the next-best P4 (₹3,396). P4 reaches only 75.2% and misses target. R2 reaches 88.1% but costs ₹8,982, which is ₹2,334 more than R1.
Trade-off: Queue balance: General is still below target at 76.3% even under R1. The plan reaches 80% overall partly because Payments rises to 84.9%. Only R2 gets General above 80% (85.3%).
Trade-off: Payments risk: the no-cost plan P1 actually drops Payments to 67.6% and lowers overall service level to 63.8%, which is worse than doing nothing (65.6%). R1 protects Payments with its own overtime rather than drawing agents from it during the day.
Trade-off: Overtime uptake: R1 depends on 14 agents accepting overtime. If fewer accept, results will fall toward P4's levels.
Watch: Watch General's service level and call volume each interval after 11:30. If overtime uptake is short or General stays well under 76%, consider stepping up to R2. Separately, check with IT whether customer login is having problems. login_issue calls are running at 1.76x forecast with no incident ticket, and a hidden outage could keep demand high beyond 15:15.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1, the no-cost rebalance: predicted 88.1% service level for 11:45–20:00, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.
General calls have run 28–51% above forecast since 10:15, with no explanation in the feeds. P1 delays the 12:15–12:45 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes. It moves 3 cross-skilled agents from payments to general for 15:00–16:00 and 1 agent for 18:00–19:00. It also turns on IVR callback on general for 15:00–16:00 and 18:00–20:00. That lifts general to 83.8% and keeps payments at 92.6%, with predicted abandons of 2.7%. It is the cheapest plan that meets policy and the target. Note that doing nothing (P0) is also predicted to reach 86.5%, but general would sit only just over target at 80.6%. P1 adds margin there for no cost.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) costs nothing and is predicted to reach 86.5% overall, but general would be at 80.6%, leaving almost no buffer if the surge grows.
Trade-off: P2 (chat deflection) costs ₹930 and lifts general to 85.2% (89.0% overall). This is a small gain over P1.
Trade-off: P4 costs ₹3,810 and P3 costs ₹7,290. They give the strongest general recovery, at 88.4% and 91.3%, and the lowest abandons, at 2.1% and 1.9%. That is extra cost the target doesn't require.
Trade-off: Moving agents off payments has little effect there: payments is predicted at 92.6% under P1 versus 92.7% with no action.
Watch: The cause of the surge is unknown. Login_issue (1.65x normal) and balance_enquiry (1.5x) are elevated, so check with IT for an unreported login or app problem. If general volume climbs further or general service level drops toward 80%, step up to P2 or P4.

explanations.plan: No-cost: lend more payments agents in the evening and spread out the 13:00 breaks
explanations.text:
Approve P1: a no-cost tweak that lifts general to 91.0% and keeps the day on target (92.8% vs 80% goal)
General calls have run 26–51% above forecast since 10:15 (855 vs 623 expected over the last 2 hours), spread evenly across call reasons, with no incident or campaign to explain it. Staffing and absence are not the issue. Even with no action, the disruption window (12:30–20:00) is predicted at 92.7%, well above the 80% target, so heavy spending isn't needed. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It costs nothing: it delays the 13:00–13:30 general breaks by 30 minutes and moves 2 cross-skilled agents from payments to general from 19:00 to 20:00. General improves from 89.2% to 91.0% and abandons fall from 1.7% to 1.5%.
Trade-off: Payments gives up some headroom: it drops from 96.0% to 94.5% because of the evening moves, still comfortably above target.
Trade-off: P2 (₹1,440 overtime) and P4 (₹900, chat deflection plus overtime) lift the overall level to about 94% and keep payments at 96.7%, but general only reaches 91.5% and 91.2%.
Trade-off: P3 (₹2,340) is the strongest at 94.5% overall, 92.7% general and 1.2% abandons, but it costs the most for a small gain over a plan that already meets target.
Trade-off: Delayed breaks push agent breaks back by 30 minutes, a minor wellbeing cost.
Watch: The cause of the surge is unknown, so check that general volume isn't climbing further. If general falls toward 80%, or payments slips after the 19:00 moves, step up to P4 (₹900) as the next cheapest option.

explanations.plan: No-cost: payments callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: turn on IVR callback for payments 18:00–20:00. It costs nothing and keeps the 16:00–20:00 window at a predicted 83.3% against the 80% target.
General calls have run about 30% over forecast all day (2,600 vs 2,003.8 so far). The rise is spread evenly across every call reason, with no customer-facing incident or campaign behind it, so there is no single cause to fix. Even so, the overall window is predicted to stay above target: 82.9% with no action and 83.3% with P1. P1 is the cheapest compliant plan that reaches 80%. It also trims predicted abandons from 4.8% to 4.5% and lifts payments to 87.9%.
Trade-off: General queue stays below target: P1 predicts general at 78.2%, slightly worse than 78.9% with no action. The overall 83.3% is propped up by payments at 87.9%.
Trade-off: P2 (₹2,424) is the targeted fix for the surge. It adds overtime for 8 general agents plus balance-enquiry chat deflection and lifts general to 92.1% and overall to 91.5%, with abandons at 2.2%.
Trade-off: P4 (₹2,280) is cheaper than P2 and reaches 92.9% overall (general 91.3%, abandons 1.8%), though it relies more on deflection.
Trade-off: P3 (₹3,660) is the strongest at 93.8% overall and 1.5% abandons, at the highest cost.
Watch: The overall margin is thin at 3.3 points, and general is already predicted to miss 80%. If general calls keep rising beyond the current 14–39% over forecast, or overall service level trends toward 80% before 18:00, switch to P4 or P2 to add general capacity.

explanations.plan: Low-cost chat deflection
explanations.text:
Approve P1: chat deflection on both queues lifts predicted service level to 81.6% for 18:15-20:00 at ₹312 extra cost.
The general queue is running well over forecast with no identified cause: 72 calls at 18:00 against 43.9 forecast (+64%), and +31% for the day. The rise is spread evenly across all call reasons. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so this is a demand problem. Service level fell to 51.4% at 18:00. Doing nothing is predicted to give 72.3% over 18:15-20:00, below the 80% target, with 6.5% abandons. P1 moves 20% of balance enquiries (general) and 20% of payment status enquiries (payments) to chat. That gives a predicted 81.6% overall with abandons at 4.2%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target, and it breaks no policy.
Trade-off: The general queue stays below target under P1 at 75.2%. Payments reaches 87.5%, and that lifts the combined figure over 80%.
Trade-off: P2 (₹2,250) uses overtime for 10 general agents and gets general to 91.7% and 86.3% overall. It costs about 7x more, and payments falls to 81.2%.
Trade-off: P4 (₹1,944) gets 88.3% overall, with general at 89.9% and abandons at 2.3%. It costs about ₹1,630 more than P1.
Trade-off: P3 (₹2,562) gives the strongest result: 93.8% overall and 1.3% abandons. It is the most expensive option.
Trade-off: P1 has almost no buffer at 81.6% against an 80% target. It also depends on customers actually accepting the move to chat.
Watch: The cause of the surge is unknown, so check the general queue's arrivals and service level after 18:30. If general stays near 75% or volume keeps climbing, add overtime (the P4 or P2 options from 18:45). Also confirm the chat team can absorb the deflected contacts.

explanations.plan: Targeted: chat deflection, callback and overtime at the worst hours
explanations.text:
Approve P2: chat deflection, callback on general and overtime 13:00-15:00 lifts the 10:30-15:15 service level to 82.3% for ₹6,576.
A dengue-driven sick wave has left payments at 33 agents against 39 planned and general at 27 against 33. Call volume and handle times are close to forecast, so this is purely a capacity gap. Doing nothing leaves the disruption window at 67.5%, with an 8.1% abandon rate. P2 moves 20% of simple enquiries to chat on both queues, adds IVR callback on general, and offers overtime to 8 agents per queue at the worst hours (13:00-15:00). That gives 82.3% overall (payments 85.7%, general 77.8%) and cuts abandons to 4.4%. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target within policy, and the rest of the day improves to 87.6%.
Trade-off: The no-cost option P1 (break shift plus callback) does not help: 66.7% in the window, slightly worse than no action, with general at 60.0%.
Trade-off: P3 adds overtime across the whole gap for ₹10,080, ₹3,504 more than P2. It reaches 84.0% overall and 3.8% abandons.
Trade-off: P3 is the only plan that gets general above 80% (81.9%). Under P2, general stays just short at 77.8% while payments carries the overall figure.
Trade-off: P2 depends on 16 agents accepting overtime and on customers taking up chat. If either falls short, results will be below the forecast.
Watch: Watch general queue service level and overtime acceptance from 13:00. If general stays well below 78% or fewer than 8 general agents accept, consider extending general overtime earlier, as in P3. Also watch for any further sick calls.

explanations.plan: No-cost rebalance
explanations.text:
Approve P1: a no-cost rebalance that lifts the 12:45-15:15 service level to 84.7%, above the 80% target.
A sickness wave, mostly dengue logged between 06:31 and 09:44, has left payments at 33 agents against 39 planned and general at 27 against 33. Call volume and handle times are close to forecast, so this is a capacity gap, not a demand spike. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just clear target at 82.8%, which leaves little margin. P1 costs nothing and gives more headroom. It delays the 12:45-13:15 breaks in both queues by 30 minutes, moves cross-skilled agents between queues as each one peaks, and switches on IVR callback on payments from 13:00 to 15:00. That raises payments to 85.2% and general to 84.0%, cuts predicted abandons from 3.4% to 2.9%, and brings rest-of-day service to 92.9%. No policy is breached.
Trade-off: P3 (overtime plus free levers) reaches 86.9% with 2.4% abandons but costs INR 2,160. That is about 2 points more for spend the target does not need.
Trade-off: P4 (overtime only) reaches 86.0% for INR 5,040. It is the most expensive option, and general only gets to 84.7%.
Trade-off: P2 costs INR 942 yet scores lower than P1 overall at 83.9%. It also leaves general close to target at 80.9%, so it shifts risk onto the general queue.
Trade-off: P1 depends on agents accepting delayed breaks and on callback take-up, rather than on paid extra staff.
Watch: Watch both queues as the 2 agents leave payments for general (13:00-14:00) and the 3 return from general to payments (14:00-15:00), making sure neither queue drops toward 80%. If more sick calls come in, be ready to offer overtime as in P3.

explanations.plan: No-cost: shift breaks and extend callback
explanations.text:
Approve P1: shift breaks and extend IVR callback on both queues. It costs nothing and is predicted to lift service level to 93.9% for 13:45-15:45, against an 80% target.
Payments is short-staffed because of a sick wave: 7 absences against a usual 2.6, 4 noted as dengue. At 13:30 there were 19 agents on the phones against 32 planned, while calls ran 9% under forecast. Doing nothing (P0) is predicted to just scrape the target at 83.7%, with payments at 81.2% and handle time running above forecast (e.g. 341s vs 287s at 13:00). That leaves little margin. P1 delays the 14:45-15:15 breaks (payments by 45 min, general by 30 min) and adds IVR callback on both queues from 15:00 to 16:00. It is predicted to bring payments to 93.7% and general to 94.3%, cut abandons from 3.0% to 1.2%, and raise the rest-of-day figure to 96.7%. There is no extra cost and no policy issues.
Trade-off: P0 costs nothing but is only predicted to reach 83.7%, and payments at 81.2% is barely above target. Any further absence or handle-time creep could tip it under.
Trade-off: P2 (INR 882) adds only 1.5 points (95.4%) by cancelling payments coaching and deflecting some enquiries to chat. It is not needed to hit the target.
Trade-off: P3 (INR 1,551) and P4 (INR 2,952, with overtime for 13 agents) reach 96.0% and 98.1%, with abandons down to 0.7% and 0.4%. These are small customer gains for real spend.
Trade-off: P1 delays general's breaks by 30 min to protect the shared load, so general agents also give up some timing flexibility. Its predicted service level still improves, from 87.0% to 94.3%.
Watch: Watch payments agents on the phones against plan, and any new sick calls. The 7 absences don't explain the full 13-agent gap, so other unplanned off-phone time may be adding to it. Also watch handle time. If payments service level drifts toward 80% before 15:00, step up to P2 (INR 882) by cancelling payments coaching and adding chat deflection.

explanations.plan: No-cost: evening callback plus afternoon move
explanations.text:
Approve P1: move 2 cross-skilled agents to payments 15:00-16:00 and run IVR callback on both queues 19:00-19:45, at no extra cost, for a predicted 88.3% service level against the 80% target.
The gap is a dengue-related sick wave, not extra demand. 11 sick absences are logged on each queue, and payments call volume is 8.7% below forecast.
