Even with no action, the disruption window (14:30-20:00) is predicted at 87.4%, already above target. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It lifts payments to 87.8% and general to 89.0%, and trims abandons from 3.4% to 3.2%, at zero cost. Moving 2 agents out of general for one hour still leaves general at 89.0%, so the other queue is not put at risk.
Trade-off: P0 (no action) also meets target at 87.4% and costs nothing, but P1 adds about a point of service level and lowers abandons for free.
Trade-off: P2 reaches 89.8% (abandon 2.7%) for INR 336, but pushes some customers to chat, which is a modest customer-experience change.
Trade-off: P3 reaches 90.2% (abandon 2.5%) for INR 1,080, and depends on 13 agents accepting overtime.
Trade-off: P4 gives the strongest result at 93.2% (abandon 1.7%) for INR 1,776, which is extra spend the 80% target does not require.
Watch: Watch payments, which has the thinnest margin at 87.8%, and check for further sick calls before the evening. If more agents drop out and payments heads toward 80%, be ready to switch to P3 overtime for 19:00-20:00. No escalation to the duty manager is needed.

explanations.plan: Payments focus: callback plus chat deflection on payments
explanations.text:
Approve P2 (callback on both queues plus 20% chat deflection on payments, ₹60), but call the duty manager: even this plan only reaches 40.6% against the 80% target for 19:45-20:00.
The gap is dengue-related sickness, not extra calls. 11 sick absences are logged on each queue against a usual 2.6 and 2.4, and volume is near or below forecast. With no action, service level is predicted at 28.8% with 30.0% abandons. P2 is the best of the options: 40.6% overall (payments 24.4%, general 70.8%), with abandons cut to 20.3%, for ₹60. R1 gives identical predictions at the same cost. Escalation is flagged because the best compliant plan is still below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager needs to decide whether anything beyond these levers, such as extra staff, is possible for the final interval.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but only reaches 32.9% and leaves abandons at 27.6%.
Trade-off: P3 and R2 cost more (₹84) and do worse (36.2%). Adding deflection on general lifts payments slightly to 25.5% but drops general from 70.8% to 59.1%.
Trade-off: P2 favours general: payments stays very weak at 24.4%, slightly below P1's 25.0%, so payments customers bear most of the remaining impact.
Watch: Watch payments service level and abandons through 19:45-20:00, and check that callbacks and chat deflection are actually taking calls off the queue. If general drops well below 70.8%, re-check with the duty manager.

explanations.plan: Full recovery with overtime
explanations.text:
Approve P3 (full recovery with overtime): best policy-compliant plan, lifting service level to 75.9% for 10:45-14:45, still short of the 80% target, for Rs 11,397.
Payments handle time has climbed from about 296 s to 556 s, most likely because of system slowness (ticket INC-20261118-1085, 30-60 s saves on chargeback/dispute screens). Volume is only modestly up. With no action, service level over 10:45-14:45 is predicted at 57.9%, with payments at 46.5% and abandons at 11.4%. P3 combines break delays, IVR callback, 20% chat deflection, overtime offers (40 agents 11:15-13:15, 5 agents 13:15-15:15) and cancelling the 15:30 coaching. That gives 75.9% overall (payments 74.6%, general 77.7%), cuts abandons to 5.6%, and lifts the rest of day to 84.1%. No plan within policy reaches 80%, so this is the best available.
Trade-off: P4 costs about the same (Rs 11,292) and is close (75.6%, abandons 5.9%). It uses no IVR callback, so customer impact is lower, but it relies on 50 overtime takers in one block and does slightly worse on payments (73.6%).
Trade-off: R1 (85.0%) and R2 (83.6%) would hit the 80% target, but both break the Rs 15,000 overtime budget (expected Rs 17,568 and Rs 17,280), so they are not allowed under policy.
Trade-off: The no-cost options P1 (54.7%) and P2 (58.2%, Rs 1,317) barely move service level. P1 is actually worse than doing nothing.
Trade-off: P3 asks customers to accept callbacks and agents to accept delayed breaks. In return, general queue holds at 77.7%, better than with no action (72.3%), so there is no risk to the other queue.
Watch: Track overtime uptake for the 11:15 block. If far fewer than 40 agents accept, payments will fall well short of 74.6%. Push for the system ticket fix: if handle time recovers, release the overtime early. If it keeps rising, the plan will underdeliver and you should involve the duty manager about the budget.

explanations.plan: Strong: concentrated overtime at the 12:00 peak
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime for 14 payments agents 12:00-13:00, plus chat deflection, delayed payments breaks and payments callback. Predicted service level is 81.7% for 11:30-14:45 at ₹2,028.
Payments handle time has risen from about 296 s to 556 s while volume is only modestly up. The likely cause is the slow chargeback/dispute screens (INC-20261118-1085), but that link is not confirmed. With no action, service level over the disruption window is predicted at 75.8% (payments 70.0%). P3 is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches the 80% target, at 81.7% overall (payments 80.0%, general 83.7%). Abandon rate falls to 4.6% from 5.7%, and the rest-of-day figure improves to 90.0%.
Trade-off: P2 costs ₹624 against ₹2,028 for P3, but reaches only 79.1% (payments 76.6%), just short of target.
Trade-off: P1 costs nothing but performs worse than doing nothing: 73.9%, with general dropping to 78.5% and abandons at 6.2%.
Trade-off: P4 is ₹132 dearer and reaches a similar 81.5%. It leaves payments lower at 78.1% and takes 2 agents from general, though general still holds at 85.6%. P3 avoids touching the general queue and in fact lifts it to 83.7%.
Trade-off: P3 depends on 14 agents accepting overtime for the 12:00 hour. Payments lands exactly on 80.0%, so there is little margin if uptake falls short.
Watch: Confirm overtime uptake before 12:00. Track payments handle time and the INC-20261118-1085 ticket. If handle time keeps climbing beyond 556 s or the slowness runs past 14:45, payments will likely fall back below target and the plan should be revisited.

explanations.plan: Split overtime across both queues with wider deflection
explanations.text:
Approve R2 (split overtime plus wider chat deflection) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best option available but still reaches only 61.6% against the 80% target for 12:45-14:45.
The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37) is driving the problem, not missing staff. Payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal, and service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandoned calls. R2 puts the known-issue IVR message on card_declined and deflects 20% of payment status, balance and refund enquiries to chat. It also offers overtime to 46 payments agents (13:15-14:45) and 5 general agents (13:15-15:00), and delays the 14:15 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes. Over the disruption window it lifts service level from 19.8% to 61.6%: payments 53.0%, general 80.5%. Abandon rate drops from 35.0% to 13.7%. Extra cost is ₹13,890, and rest-of-day service level is 81.4%. Escalation is flagged because even this plan is predicted at 62%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). No plan reaches target while the outage continues.
Trade-off: Against P3 (₹14,784, 58.1%) and P4 (₹15,414, 51.8%), R2 costs less and performs better.
Trade-off: Against R1 (₹13,344, 57.3%), R2 costs ₹546 more for about 4 points more service level. It is also the only plan that brings general to 80.5%; R1 leaves general at 74.6%.
Trade-off: The no-cost P1 (26.7%) and low-cost P2 (₹924, 28.0%) leave payments below 10% and abandon rates above 20%.
Trade-off: R2 depends on enough agents accepting overtime (46 payments, 5 general) and on customers actually moving to chat. Shortfalls on either will pull results below 61.6%.
Watch: Watch overtime take-up by 13:15 and the card_declined call volume. If the gateway fix is delayed beyond 14:45, or payments service level is not climbing toward 53% by about 13:45, go back to the duty manager on extending overtime or adding further measures. Also confirm general stays near 80% once its breaks are moved.

explanations.plan: Strong: spend remaining overtime budget on the 14:00 peak plus free levers
explanations.text:
Approve P3: overtime on the 14:00 peak plus free levers lifts service level to 80.8% for 13:30-15:30, meeting the 80% target for INR 2,835.
The problem is extra calls from the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37), not missing staff. Card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal, payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, and service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandons. P3 offers overtime to 26 payments agents for 14:00-15:00. It also delays payments breaks by 45 minutes and runs IVR callbacks from 13:30-15:30. From 15:00 it moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments, plays the outage message on payments, and cancels coaching from 15:30-16:00. Predicted results for the window: 80.8% overall (payments 76.7%, general 89.3%) and abandons down to 4.0%. Rest-of-day rises to 89.4%. It is the only option that reaches the target, and it breaks no policy.
Trade-off: Cost: P3 costs INR 2,835 and uses the remaining overtime budget. P1 is free but only reaches 69.0%, and P2 costs INR 324 but only reaches 74.3%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: abandons fall to 4.0% under P3, against 7.2% with no action, 6.3% under P1 and 5.6% under P2. Payments still sits below target at 76.7%, so the overall target is met mainly through general's 89.3%.
Trade-off: Other queue: moving 3 agents out of general from 15:00 costs it a little. General is predicted at 89.3% under P3 versus 90.1% under P2, still well above target.
Trade-off: Staff: breaks are delayed and coaching is cancelled. Overtime depends on enough of the 26 agents accepting.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 14:00 and payments service level through the peak. If take-up is low, or the gateway outage runs past 15:30 and card_declined volumes stay high, payments will fall short and the plan should be revisited. Escalation is not flagged at this point.

explanations.plan: Maximum no-overtime recovery
explanations.text:
Approve R1 (Maximum no-overtime recovery) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best available plan but only reaches 64.3% service level against the 80% target for 14:45-16:45.
The gap is caused by the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37), not missing staff. Payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, and card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal. R1 combines delayed breaks, cancelled coaching, IVR outage messaging, chat deflection on both queues, payments callback, and moving 4 cross-skilled agents to payments from 16:00. It is predicted to lift the window from 48.2% (no action) to 64.3%, cut abandons from 13.4% to 9.1%, and bring rest-of-day to 79.9%, at an extra cost of INR 2,358. No plan reaches 80%. Escalation is flagged (ESC-02) because even the best compliant plan is below the 70% escalation line.
